title: Two Buffers Eroded: A Structural Analysis of Japan's Fertility Decline through Social Ties Erosion and Middle-Class Income Suppression

detail.title: Two Buffers Eroded: A Structural Analysis of Japan's Fertility Decline through Social Ties Erosion and Middle-Class Income Suppression
detail.abstract: Japan's total fertility rate (TFR) has declined from 2.13 in 1970 to 1.20 in 2024, yet conventional analyses fail to recognize that this decline operates through two distinct mechanisms in two distinct time periods. From the 1970s through the early 2000s, married couples maintained a stable completed cohort fertility (CCF) of approximately 2.20; the TFR decline reflected falling marriage rates alone. Then, in 2005, CCF began to fall for the first time, declining from 2.23 (2002) to 1.90 (2021). This paper proposes a "Two Buffers" framework. Stage One (marriage decline) reflects the erosion of the social buffer-the community-embedded relationships that historically supported marriage formation. The post-1975 transition from collective employment to individual employment severed the social ties that once accompanied rural-to-urban migration, leaving young adults economically rational but socially isolated. The empirical signature is striking: during the collective employment era (1955-1972), urbanization correlated positively with marriage rates (r = +0.88); after 1975, the same correlation reversed sharply (r =-0.86). Stage Two (within-marriage fertility decline) reflects the erosion of the economic buffer-specifically, the option for one parent to focus on childcare without working full-time. The decline of middle-class real takehome pay since 1992, driven by cumulative tax and social insurance changes, eliminated this option. The 13-year time lag in CCF measurement (which samples couples married 15-19 years prior, with childbearing typically completed within 5 years) explains why the 1992 inflection point manifests as the 2005 CCF decline. International comparison reveals that this Two Buffers framework generalizes: Korea exhibits both buffers severely eroded (extreme capital concentration plus housing price explosion) yielding a TFR of 0.72; Italy shows similar patterns; Germany's federal structure preserves the social buffer; France and Sweden compensate the economic buffer through family policy. We conclude that conventional Japanese fertility policies-aimed at urban childcare expansion and child allowances-address neither buffer and will fail. Required reforms operate on a 30-year horizon and address structural causes: regional revitalization to restore social buffers, and structural income reform (the "Five Pillars" framework) to restore economic buffers. Without such reform, Japan will likely continue along Korea's trajectory.

title: Climate Risk Assessment of Coastal Rice Farming in Eastern India
affiliations: Kerala Agricultural University, Justus Liebig University Giessen, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Justus Liebig University Giessen and College of Agriculture

detail.title: Climate Risk Assessment of Coastal Rice Farming in Eastern India
detail.abstract: Odisha, located on the eastern coast of India, is among the most climate vulnerable states, where nearly 40 per cent of the population is affected by floods, cyclones and drought. Among the affected, the worst off are the rice farmers, since their livelihoods are closely linked with vulnerable ecosystems and unpredictable weather. Considering these realities, the present study aims to assess the climate risk faced by rice farmers in the flood and cyclone prone districts of Puri and Ganjam by calculating the Climate Risk IndexFlood (CRIF) and evaluating its robustness through sensitivity analysis. The CRIF integrates three dimensions of risk i.e. hazard, vulnerability, and exposure, under which 13 major components and 68 indicators were identified. Primary data were collected from 256 rice farmers using a structured interview schedule. The CRIF showed that although Puri and Ganjam recorded nearly identical values for hazard (0.590 and 0.563) and exposure (0.471 and 0.453), they differed in vulnerability, i.e., sensitivity and adaptive capacity. Puri had higher sensitivity (0.466) and lower risk to adaptive capacity (0.377), while Ganjam performed vice versa (0.341 and 0.441, respectively). The major components indicate that farmers in Puri are more vulnerable due to poor drainage, saline intrusion, and prolonged water logging, whereas in Ganjam, frequent flash floods and higher dependence on erratic rainfall are critical concerns. The leave-one-out sensitivity analysis validated the robustness of the CRIF, highlighting that water and natural disaster impact components, significantly affected overall risk while health and food factors had comparatively minor effects.

title: Data-Driven Surrogate Models for Real-Time Fatigue Monitoring of Chain Mooring Lines in Floating Wind Turbines
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, PEAK Wind, Technical University of Denmark and PEAK Wind

detail.title: Data-Driven Surrogate Models for Real-Time Fatigue Monitoring of Chain Mooring Lines in Floating Wind Turbines
detail.abstract: As the first commercial floating wind projects are about to enter the market, Operations and Maintenance, currently 30% of the overall cost of energy, remains a major challenge, especially for floating wind due to the logistical complexity of deep, remote offshore locations. A significant part of recent developments therefore focuses on condition monitoring of mooring systems, where fatigue damage is a leading failure cause. However, the high cost and reliability issues of the sensors prevent their adoption at a commercial scale. This paper presents a machine learning surrogate model methodology for real-time prediction of hourly fatigue damage accumulation in catenary chain mooring lines, based on five metocean variables wind speed, wave height, wave period, wind direction, and wind–wave misalignment. The model incorporates effects of corrosion and mean loads, which both significantly impact chain fatigue life. A synthetic, site-agnostic training database was generated using OpenFAST simulations. A gradient-boosted decision tree achieves an R^2-value of 0.928, with the residual error attributed primarily to seed-to-seed uncertainty. Prediction time under 0.01 s makes the model suitable for real-time asset monitoring and reliability-based design optimization. Overall, the proposed approach provides a computationally efficient and accurate method for accounting for key environmental factors influencing fatigue.

title: Credibility Capital, Institutions, and the Long-Term Credit Cycle

detail.title: Credibility Capital, Institutions, and the Long-Term Credit Cycle
detail.abstract: Why do some highly indebted countries retain market confidence for long periods, while others face acute funding stress at much lower levels of debt? Existing explanations typically emphasize either fiscal fundamentals or institutional quality. This paper argues that the relevant object is their interaction through a slow-moving stock of credibility capital. Credibility capital is produced by the persistent success of institutions in preserving nominal and financial order. should display lower spread sensitivity to debt in normal times, but more abrupt nonlinear repricing near the frontier. The framework provides a unified theory of sovereign fragility, institutional persistence, and the long-term credit cycle. More broadly, it advances a new view of institutions. Beyond shaping productivity, incentives, and political order, institutions also produce a stock of macro-financial credibility that governs how long leverage can expand before disorder emerges.

title: The Flexibility Window: India’s Coal Minimum Load Mandate Increases System Costs at Current and Projected RE Penetration​
affiliations: Independent Researcher and University of Oxford - Smith School of Enterprise and the Environment

detail.title: The Flexibility Window: India’s Coal Minimum Load Mandate Increases System Costs at Current and Projected RE Penetration​
detail.abstract: India mandates that coal plants reduce minimum technical load (MTL) from 55% to 40% by 2030 to accommodate renewable energy (RE). Using a 125-plant, 15-minute resolution unit commitment model across 21 scenarios, we find this mandate increases system costs at most RE levels. The flexibility window, where lower MTL saves money, is narrow (6–12.5% RE penetration), bounded below by part-load heat rate penalties and above by increased curtailment where parked thermal capacity blocks RE absorption, increasing curtailment by up to 1,886 GWh/year. At RE penetrations matching India's projected 2030 trajectory (~22%), the modelled fleet’s costs rise by Rs 11.8–22.9 billion ($131–255 million) per year; scaled to India's full 223 GW coal fleet on a cost-tier-exposure basis, the indicative national impact is Rs 49–102 Bn ($545M–$1.13B) per year. Although static NPV is positive at one RE level (12.5%), India’s projected RE growth would carry the system through that window within 1–2 years, leaving the retrofit unrecovered along the actual deployment trajectory. Fleet-wide thermal flexibility mandates may thus yield diminishing or negative economic returns as power systems approach deep decarbonization.​

title: Road transportation PPP project resilience analytical framework:a system thinking and modelling
affiliations: Yunnan Agricultural University, Yunnan Agricultural University, Yunnan Agricultural University and Yunnan Agricultural University

detail.title: Road transportation PPP project resilience analytical framework:a system thinking and modelling
detail.abstract: Enhancing the resilience of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) projects is of great significance for ensuring the quality and efficiency of road transportation infrastructure and public service provision. However, existing research has not fully explored the dynamic feedback mechanisms underlying PPP resilience. Therefore, drawing on systems thinking, this paper proposes an analytical framework that integrates the dual perspectives of the crisis life cycle and stakeholders, encompassing driving factors, stakeholder satisfaction, and decision-making behavioral processes. This study validates the analytical framework and identifies key resilience pathways, providing robust evidence to address the challenges in resilience management of PPP projects.

title: Green Accounting and Financial Performance of Rural Banks in Ghana: Exploring the Mediating Roles of Earnings Management and Corporate Governance, and the Moderating Effect of Firm Age
affiliations: Valley View University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Valley View University

detail.title: Green Accounting and Financial Performance of Rural Banks in Ghana: Exploring the Mediating Roles of Earnings Management and Corporate Governance, and the Moderating Effect of Firm Age
detail.abstract: The research examined the main relationship between green accounting and the financial performance of rural and community banks (RCBs) in Ghana, investigating the mediating roles of earnings management and corporate governance, as well as the moderating effects of firm age on this mediation. The design of the study was a quantitative cross-sectional. Both primary and secondary data were utilized for the study. The data were analyzed using regression and the process macro to examine both indirect and conditional effect paths within the conceptual framework. The findings show that there is small significant relationship between green accounting and financial performance. Furthermore, there was no indirect effect of corporate governance and earnings management on the relationship between green accounting and financial performance. Moreover, the influence of green accounting on financial performance was not significantly affected by firm age through mediators such as earnings management, board size, independent audit committees, or board gender diversity. The findings indicate that policymakers ought to encourage green accounting, guarantee effective corporate governance, and implement succession planning for boards of directors. Through environmental reporting and disclosures, the study promotes these banks' long-term sustainability and viability while ensuring that stakeholders benefit from enhanced accounting information.

title: Transferable rotation scheduling for agricultural irrigation delivery using a weighted composite objective and a sigmoid-adaptive genetic algorithm: two oasis irrigation-district case studies
affiliations: Shihezi University, Shihezi University, Shihezi University, Shihezi University, Shihezi University, Shihezi University and Shihezi University

detail.title: Transferable rotation scheduling for agricultural irrigation delivery using a weighted composite objective and a sigmoid-adaptive genetic algorithm: two oasis irrigation-district case studies
detail.abstract: Arid agricultural irrigation districts depend on timely and reliable water delivery to cropland, yet rotational canal operation often suffers from conveyance losses, rigid hydraulic constraints, and unstable trunk-canal regulation. To support practical irrigation service for farmland, this study develops a transferable rotation-scheduling framework based on a weighted composite objective that jointly minimizes total seepage loss across trunk–lateral canal systems and the variance of trunk-canal gross discharge, subject to strict demand-satisfaction and hydraulic-capacity constraints. An improved sigmoid-adaptive genetic algorithm (SIGGA) is proposed as the solver to enhance feasibility attainment, reliability, and convergence stability through feasibility-first selection and adaptive genetic operators. Using consistent modeling assumptions and evaluation criteria, the framework is tested in two representative oasis agricultural irrigation districts in northwest China to evaluate robustness and transferability across contrasting canal structures and water-demand levels. In the Zhangye benchmark (Xijun Irrigation District), the optimized schedule completes one rotation in 10 days, 60% shorter than the manual 25-day plan, while maintaining stable trunk-canal discharge with maximum, minimum, and mean values of 2.44, 2.13, and 2.31 m³ s⁻¹, respectively, and a discharge variance of 0.0064. Total gross diversion, gross lateral delivery, and net field delivery are 1.9958×10⁶, 1.7802×10⁶, and 1.6820×10⁶ m³, respectively, corresponding to a total seepage loss of 0.3138×10⁶ m³ and a canal water utilization coefficient of 0.833. Under the same evaluation criterion, SIGGA reduces total leakage by 3.8–56.3% relative to VEGA, MOPSO, and GSPSO in Zhangye. In the Shihezi case, SIGGA further achieves shorter rotations and lower leakage under both irrigation quotas, indicating more timely and reliable irrigation delivery to cropland. These results show that the proposed framework can provide practical decision support for agricultural water delivery in arid oasis farming systems, while maintaining robust performance across districts without case-specific retuning.

title: Risk analysis in LPG tanker truck loading: application of the MADS-MOSAR method
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Risk analysis in LPG tanker truck loading: application of the MADS-MOSAR method
detail.abstract: The main energy sources of our day are petroleum and gas, which hold a vital position in modern industry. In Algeria, hydrocarbons are essential to the country's economic development. However, even though gas is an essential resource, improper management of it can pose serious risks with potentially disastrous effects for people, infrastructure, and the environment.,Our study's primary goal is to analyze the industrial risks associated with gas distribution inside the company GPL NAFTAL. In order to bring these risks down to acceptable levels in the station where city trucks are charged, we are working to identify and manage them. In order to determine the risks, dangers, and damages, we have chosen the MADS-MOSAR method, which will enable us to determine the degree of protection linked to each risk in the various sub-systems. Then, using the identified risks, this approach will lead us to suggest protective measures tailored to each subsystem.

title: The Two-Echelon Time-Dependent Green Location-Routing Problem
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Lausanne, Eindhoven University of Technology (TUE) and Eindhoven University of Technology (TUE)

detail.title: The Two-Echelon Time-Dependent Green Location-Routing Problem
detail.abstract: This study presents the Two-Echelon Time-Dependent Green Location-Routing Problem (2E-TDGLRP), a model designed to optimize urban logistics by determining the optimal locations for intermediate hubs, vehicle routes, and delivery schedules, while minimizing both economic and environmental costs. To account for varying road conditions throughout the day, the model incorporates a time-dependent speed function that reflects the impact of traffic congestion on urban transportation. The research highlights the two-way relationship between logistics operations and traffic congestion, as logistics activities both affect and contribute to congestion. A mixed-integer linear programming model is developed for 2E-TDGLRP, incorporating novel variables and constraints that enhance scalability for large-scale problem instances. To further improve computational efficiency, a matheuristic algorithm is introduced, which first decomposes the multilevel decision-making process and constructs delivery routes through customer clustering. This is followed by an allocation refinement step to improve the solution. Results demonstrate significant gains in both computational speed and solution quality, highlighting the advantages of the enhanced formulation and matheuristic approach. The findings offer valuable insights into the complex trade-offs inherent in urban logistics planning. In particular, our results reveal that although time-dependent planning increases operational costs for logistics service providers, it substantially improves on-time deliveries and reduces emissions in urban areas.

title: CAN NYKAA GO GLOBAL?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: CAN NYKAA GO GLOBAL?
detail.abstract:
This report explores whether it actually makes sense for Nykaa (FSN E-Commerce Ventures) to go global. To find the answer, I’ve stress-tested their numbers against US giants using a comparable valuation framework, a deep dive into unit economics, and three specific financial models for entering the US market.

Key Findings:

  • The Valuation Gap: Nykaa is currently trading at a massive 156x EV/EBITDA. This essentially means the market is pricing in a "perfect" future. However, Nykaa’s 5.9% EBITDA margin is way behind US peers like Ulta (17.2%) and e.l.f. (17.6%). It’s a classic valuation trap—the same one that led to a 70% crash in e.l.f.’s stock when their growth started to normalize.
  • The Cost of Entry: In India, Nykaa spends about $0.69 to get a customer. In the US, that cost jumps to $67 (based on Ulta’s benchmarks). That is a 97x increase. If Nykaa tries a direct entry, they’ll be bleeding cash for at least three years before they ever see a return on that investment.
  • The Only Path Forward: Out of the three scenarios I modelled, only one actually adds value. An asset-light licensing partnership would only cost $5M to set up and would be profitable from Year 1. My model shows this path could add $2,704M to Nykaa’s Enterprise Value by the third year.
    Final Recommendation: Nykaa should avoid the temptation to build from scratch or buy a US company right now; it would just destroy shareholder value. Instead, they should license their owned brands (Kay Beauty, Nykaa Beauty) to an established US distributor. A full-scale direct entry only makes financial sense once their domestic EBITDA margins hit the 12-15% mark—which is likely a 3 to 5-year goal.

title: Objective Selection in Many-Objective Optimization via Conditioning-Based Analysis of Objective Redundancy

detail.title: Objective Selection in Many-Objective Optimization via Conditioning-Based Analysis of Objective Redundancy
detail.abstract: Many-objective optimization problems often include objectives that appear redundant because they are influenced by the same decision variables. Most objective selection methods use statistical dependence measures, but these measures do not distinguish between dependencies induced by shared decision variables and residual relationships between objectives. This work proposes a conditioning-based objective selection method, inspired by causal reasoning, to identify compact and interpretable objective subsets. Each objective is modeled as a function of the decision variables, and redundancy is assessed from the residual dependencies that remain after conditioning. The method is evaluated on DTLZ and WFG benchmark problems and on an injection molding case study. The results show that conditioning substantially reduces apparent objective dependence; in the injection molding case, mean dependence decreased from 0.461 to 0.192. The case study also shows that thermal objectives act as upstream descriptors of the process, while, in this dataset and under the sampled processing window, shrinkage and warpage provide limited additional independent information once thermal descriptors and decision variables are accounted for. A regime-specific analysis further indicates that the gate variable defines distinct process regimes. Overall, the results show that conditioning-based selection, combined with engineering knowledge, provides an interpretable framework for objective reduction in complex engineering optimization problems.

title: Catalytic Digital Infrastructure: Reconfiguring Multilateral Development Bank Pipelines Through Small-Scale Technical Assistance and Governance Innovation

detail.title: Catalytic Digital Infrastructure: Reconfiguring Multilateral Development Bank Pipelines Through Small-Scale Technical Assistance and Governance Innovation

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not contain any studies with human or animal subjects performed by any of the authors.
declarations.funderStatement: The research is not funded.

detail.abstract:
This paper investigates how small-to-medium catalytic technical assistance initiatives can be strategically designed to align with Multilateral Development Bank (MDB) priorities, generate scalable investment pipelines, and position civil society-innovation networks as regional knowledge intermediaries. Drawing on policy analysis, comparative case review, and strategic framework design, the study examines the digital-green governance nexus and identifies a persistent project preparation gap that constrains infrastructure financing in emerging economies. 
The research demonstrates that early-stage readiness programs, when structured around anchor pilot concepts, blended finance logic, and transparent digital governance, can achieve leverage ratios of 1:20-50, effectively transforming technical assistance into investment pipelines. Contrary to conventional MDB paradigms that prioritize hard infrastructure deployment and top-down policy harmonization, this paper argues for a governance-first, ecosystem-driven approach that embeds climate alignment, market competition safeguards, and AI transparency into digital infrastructure planning. 
Strategic recommendations are provided for the Green Transformation and Sustainability Network (GXS) to operationalize a Sustainable Digital Infrastructure Readiness Program (SDIRP) that functions as a catalytic platform for MDB engagement. The paper contributes a novel "catalytic readiness" framework to development finance literature and offers actionable architecture for scaling small initiatives into regional investment pipelines.

title: « FROM THE CODE OF HONOR TO THE STATE NORM: AN ANALYSIS OF LEGAL PLURALISM IN THE WORKS OF CHUCK NORRIS AS A REGULATORY MODEL IN SPACES OF ANOMIE. »
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: « FROM THE CODE OF HONOR TO THE STATE NORM: AN ANALYSIS OF LEGAL PLURALISM IN THE WORKS OF CHUCK NORRIS AS A REGULATORY MODEL IN SPACES OF ANOMIE. »

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: This article deepens the study of the "Vigilante" figure in Chuck Norris's work by analyzing it through the lens of critical legal pluralism. While previous research focused on the act of intervention, this study explores the normative dimension of the work: how the hero generates an autonomous legal system where the State is failing. Drawing on the work of Kleinhans and Macdonald (1997), the author demonstrates that the "Code of Honor" embodied by Norris does not constitute an absence of rules, but rather a rigorous substitute norm. The analysis reveals that in spaces of anomie, positive law loses its binding force in favor of natural law based on efficiency and the immediate protection of the vulnerable. The article proposes the concept of "De Facto Mediation," a form of regulation by authority where the third party is no longer a mere facilitator, but a coercive guarantor of social order. This "Regulation by Honor" model offers innovative perspectives for legal diplomacy and conflict resolution in areas of contested sovereignty. In conclusion, the study suggests that the recognition of informal legal orders is a crucial step for institutional resilience in major crisis contexts, transforming a popular culture icon into a laboratory for reflection on the reconstruction of the Rule of Law.

title: Are Labor-Controlled Firms More Innovative? Evidence from a Regression Discontinuity Design
affiliations: Syracuse University - Whitman School of Management

detail.title: Are Labor-Controlled Firms More Innovative? Evidence from a Regression Discontinuity Design
detail.abstract: We examine how labor representation on corporate boards affects innovation. Exploiting German co-determination law, which requires one-third (one-half) labor-elected directors in firms above 500 (2,000) employees, we implement a regression discontinuity design using administrative employer-inventor-patent data. Crossing either threshold raises innovative productivity, measured as the forward citation-weighted number of patents per firm, by about 20-25%. This increase is driven by more patents, while forward citations do not rise and decline significantly at the parity cutoff, indicating a shift toward more incremental, less path-breaking inventions. Additional evidence shows that labor-controlled firms insure workers against adverse labor market shocks, lengthen inventors' employment spells, and offer wage incentives that reward patent quantity rather than quality. Overall, labor representation expands the number of patented inventions but dilutes their average citation impact, reallocating innovative effort in labor-controlled firms from path-breaking to incremental projects.

Asset Management and the Preservation of Labor In any high-capital industry, the preservation of the primary asset is a biological and financial necessity.

title: A Novel Hybrid Lyapunov-Reinforcement Learning Framework for Intelligent Resource Orchestration in Software-Defined Fog-Edge Networks
affiliations: The University of Tokyo, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), National University Singapore and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)

detail.title: A Novel Hybrid Lyapunov-Reinforcement Learning Framework for Intelligent Resource Orchestration in Software-Defined Fog-Edge Networks
detail.abstract: The convergence of fog computing, edge computing, and software-defined networking (SDN) establishes a powerful platform for dynamic resource orchestration in latency-critical distributed systems. This paper presents a hybrid machine learning-driven framework that leverages distributed optimization to intelligently orchestrate task offloading and adaptive resource provisioning across heterogeneous fog-edge infrastructures. By seamlessly integrating Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty techniques with reinforcement learning and predictive analytics, while exploiting SDN's programmable centralized control plane, the proposed scheme achieves substantial reductions in end-to-end latency and energy consumption while strictly satisfying quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. The decision problem is rigorously formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) and solved via a scalable heuristic relaxation combined with convex approximation, ensuring both optimality guarantees and computational tractability at large network scales. Extensive trace-driven simulations on realistic multi-tier fog-edge-cloud topologies demonstrate that the framework consistently outperforms conventional centralized MINLP and linear programming baselines across key performance metrics, including latency, energy efficiency, throughput, and queue stability. These results confirm the efficacy of the hybrid Lyapunov-reinforcement learning paradigm for next-generation intelligent and sustainable edge networking ecosystems.

title: ViDA and the Transformation of EU VAT

detail.title: ViDA and the Transformation of EU VAT
detail.abstract: The VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package is the most significant reform of EU VAT since 1993. This paper analyzes ViDA's capacity to build the foundation for a definitive VAT regime, a project that has been set aside indefinitely. It shows that ViDA leaves Member States' VAT rates, exemptions, and compliance thresholds untouched and allows them to implement the infrastructure in different ways, with varying levels of enforcement capacity. ViDA largely preserves the existing transitional VAT system, and whether a fully unified ("definitive") VAT regime can emerge will depend more on future political agreement and closer administrative coordination among Member States than on the implementation of digital reporting infrastructures.

title: Fee Abolition, Compulsory Schooling, and Later-life Mortality:  Evidence from a School Reform in Japan
affiliations: Hitotsubashi University and Simon Fraser University (SFU)

detail.title: Fee Abolition, Compulsory Schooling, and Later-life Mortality:  Evidence from a School Reform in Japan
detail.abstract: Prior studies exploiting compulsory-schooling laws generally find null mortality effects, potentially reflecting complier composition: mandated individuals may have low marginal returns to schooling. Using a multi-cutoff regression discontinuity design, we estimate the later-life mortality effects of Japan’s 1947 school reform, which abolished fees and extended compulsory schooling to secondary school. Across three adjacent school-entry cutoffs, affected cohorts were exposed to one, two, or three years of fee relief, with only the youngest also subject to the mandate. We find that the reform increased schooling by 0.12–0.21 years, yet mortality through age 87 does not decline at any cutoff, ruling out reductions larger than 1.1% of baseline mortality. Notably, effects remain null even at the fee-abolition margin, which is more likely than mandates to induce students with higher marginal returns, suggesting that null mortality effects at the secondary-school margin may reflect limited health returns rather than mandate-induced complier composition.

title: A Formal Model of the Cantillon Effect

detail.title: A Formal Model of the Cantillon Effect
detail.abstract: Nearly three centuries after Richard Cantillon first described how the route of monetary injection determines its distributional incidence, no reduced-form formal model of the mechanism exists. This paper provides the first. We construct a minimal benchmark in which agents at different topological distances from the injection point receive new money at staggered times, and the price level adjusts with a lag toward an endogenously determined notional value. The model yields two results. First, long-run flow neutrality holds: every agent's real income eventually returns to its pre-injection baseline. Second, flow neutrality coexists with permanent stock redistribution: agents who receive money before prices begin to rise accumulate persistent real-income gains, while those who receive it later suffer persistent losses. A numerical illustration with plausible parameter values shows cumulative welfare changes of $$+498.87$$ and $$-184.76$$ for the early and late receivers, respectively, despite identical long-run real incomes. The flow/stock distinction — the limit versus the sum — is the paper's conceptual contribution to monetary theory. Standard analyses that evaluate monetary expansion solely by long-run neutrality miss the entire distributional dimension of the transition path.

title: An EMD-Based Modified BP Neural Network Model for Accurate Tidal Prediction
affiliations: Dalian Maritime University, Dalian Maritime University, Dalian Maritime University, Dalian Maritime University and Dalian Maritime University

detail.title: An EMD-Based Modified BP Neural Network Model for Accurate Tidal Prediction
detail.abstract: Accurate tidal prediction faces many intrinsic difficulties, such as nonlinearity, non-stationarity, and multi-factor coupling, limiting the prediction accuracy of conventional methods. In this paper, we present an empirical mode decomposition-back propagation (EMD-BP) hybrid model for high-accuracy tidal forecasting. Initially, the original tidal time series is adaptively decomposed by EMD into a series of intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) and a residual component, obtaining signals at various temporal resolutions that reflect the multi-dimensional dynamic information of the tidal signal. Subsequently, a BP neural network integrated with the sliding time window (STW) technique is employed to predict each decomposed subsequence independently by taking advantage of its strong nonlinear mapping ability to detect small changes in the tidal data. Finally, all the results of the predicted decomposed subsequences are reconstructed to produce the final tidal level prediction. Using hourly tidal data of two U.S. tidal stations (La Jolla, CA, and Charleston, SC), the proposed model outperforms the traditional harmonic analysis (HA) method and the standalone BP models across key evaluation indicators. The proposed EMD-BP model offers a dependable approach for tidal prediction, which can provide technical support for the safety of marine transportation, coastal engineering construction, and the sustainable development of marine resources.

title: An Autoencoder--Transfer Learning Framework for Ship Structural Damage Detection under Multiple Domain Shift Scenarios
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: An Autoencoder--Transfer Learning Framework for Ship Structural Damage Detection under Multiple Domain Shift Scenarios
detail.abstract: Autoencoder-based structural health monitoring (SHM) learns a healthy-data manifold tied to structural and sensor conditions; service-time changes invalidate this baseline. Existing autoencoder–transfer learning (AE-TL) studies predominantly adopt supervised classification in rotating machinery, while unsupervised studies each address only a single shift type. This paper presents the first unsupervised AE-TL framework for ship SHM, fine-tuning a pre-trained autoencoder on a small new-domain healthy dataset without damage labels. The framework is tested on a bulk carrier finite element model under three domain shifts: structural repair, sensor relocation, and non-uniform sensor drift. A differential learning-rate Adam strategy, determined through ablation in Section 6.2, assigns 10⁻⁵ to the encoder and 10⁻³ to the decoder to preserve the pre-trained representation while recalibrating shifted channels. Adapted models achieve 5.0-to-5.7-fold lower reconstruction error than random-initialization training and reach max-channel AUC = 0.953–0.993, outperforming both the unadapted source model and the scratch-trained baseline across all three scenarios. A unified difficulty–data-size ablation reveals scenario-specific adaptation costs, with tens to a few hundred new healthy samples typically sufficient. Cumulative multi-domain adaptation remains effective under the tested training budget and is path-independent, with final-domain detection depending only on the last-trained domain.

title: Trade Hubs and the Uneven Gains from Globalization: Urban and Rural Disparities from Satellite Nighttime Lights Data
affiliations: University of Tsukuba

detail.title: Trade Hubs and the Uneven Gains from Globalization: Urban and Rural Disparities from Satellite Nighttime Lights Data

declarations.funderStatement: S.Y. appreciates the financial support from MEXT Scholarship.

detail.abstract:
This study examines how export growth affects local economic activity and rural–urban in-
equality, using nighttime luminosity as a proxy for income. We construct bilateral export values for each country pair from 1997 to 2020, covering countries with at least one major port. Trade-hub areas are defined as locations within a 50 km radius (30 km in robustness checks) of each country’s three largest ports and three largest international airports. To ac- count for zero export values, we estimate a gravity equation using Poisson pseudo–maximum likelihood. To address export endogeneity, we employ a two-stage least squares (2SLS)
framework in which export volumes are instrumented using predicted trade from a dynamic
gravity equation that captures exogenous variation arising from changes in transportation costs across modes. To avoid mechanically capturing lights from ports and airports them-selves, we exclude nighttime luminosity within a 3 km radius of each port and airport.

Our results show that a 1 percent increase in exports raises nighttime luminosity by 0.31 percent in trade-hub areas and by 0.06 percent in non-trade-hub areas, widening the rural–urban income gap by an estimated 15–17 percent between 1997 and 2018. Export growth also increases nighttime luminosity per capita by 0.19 percent in trade-hub areas and by 0.04 percent elsewhere, although modest migration into trade hubs partially offsets per-capita gains. Overall, the results indicate that export growth has heterogeneous spatial effects, with
substantially larger gains in trade-hub areas, thereby contributing to widening rural–urban
income disparities.

title: Propagation of uncertainties in a CFD simulation of the VVER1000 in-vessel flow based on Deterministic Sampling and Metalog distribution
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Framatome SA and Framatome SA

detail.title: Propagation of uncertainties in a CFD simulation of the VVER1000 in-vessel flow based on Deterministic Sampling and Metalog distribution

keywords.keywords: Uncertainty Quantification - CFD - Turbulent mixing - Deterministic Sampling - Metalog Distribution

detail.abstract: The work presented in this document focuses on the propagation of inputs uncertainty through Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations. Due to the high computational cost related to CFD, Monte-Carlo or Random sampling is rejected, and the highly effective and low-cost propagation method, Deterministic Sampling (DS,) is selected. DS relies on deterministically chosen samples named ensembles aiming to represent the statistical moments of random variables (RV). Ensembles of increasing complexity and thus increasing size can be constructed. One question arises around the minimal requirement of represented statistical moments, and ensembles of increasing complexity ranging from 8 samples to 25 samples related to four RV are here examined. Moreover, Deterministic Sampling provides only the statistical moments of the output result distribution but no information regarding its probability density function (PDF) is available. For overcoming this limitation, the use of the Metalog PDF model calibrated on statistical moments issued by DS is here proposed. Three application cases are here evaluated: firstly, two nonlinear analytical case, on which the DS Metalog chain results obtained with different ensembles are benchmarked to quasi-analytical solutions and alternative uncertainty propagation methods, and eventually, on a CFD simulation of Kozloduy-6 VVER-1000 mixing experiment with a propagation of four uncertain inputs. For this application, an ensemble of eight samples and a more complete ensemble of twenty-five samples are used for the evaluation of quantiles on the temperature field calculated with CFD for which similar results are obtained.

title: The Effect of Access to Information and Communication Technology (ICT) on Income Distribution in Provinces of Iran
affiliations: and University of Mazandaran

detail.title: The Effect of Access to Information and Communication Technology (ICT) on Income Distribution in Provinces of Iran
detail.abstract: This paper aims to examine the effects of access to information and communication technology (ICT) on income distribution in Iranian provinces, with an emphasis on the per capita income and education. Using economic theories, the relationship between access to ICT and income distribution was evaluated within a dynamic panel model by use of Generalized method of moments (GMM) during 2010-2015. The results indicate that access to ICT significantly reduces income inequality. In addition, education as a complement factor for ICT, strengthens the positive impact of access to ICT on reducing income inequality. This impact is greater among provinces having lower GDP per capita than nation-wide GDP per capita. Furthermore, inflation rate leads to an increase in income inequality, and government spending is not an influential factor in the proper distribution of income in the provinces of Iran.

title: The Effect of Volatility of Unpredicted Exchange Rate Movement and Labor Market Regidity on Export
affiliations: University of Tsukuba

detail.title: The Effect of Volatility of Unpredicted Exchange Rate Movement and Labor Market Regidity on Export
detail.abstract: Exchange rate is one of the most volatile macroeconomic price variables. The fluctuations in the exchange rate generate volatility in the profits of firms and reduce the incentives of firms to enter the market or to expand their capacity. In response to exchange rate volatility firms may reduce labor costs to mitigate the negative impact through firing workers, reducing the work hours, eliminating severance pay, etc. However, labor market rigidity restricts a firm’s ability to implement such adjustment, consequently amplifying the negative impact of exchange rate volatility on economic outcomes. This study contributes to literature by investigating the interaction effects of exchange rate volatility and labor market rigidity on industrial exports growth. We utilized a country-industry-level disaggregated panel dataset covering 17 industries for the span of 14 years (2005-2018) across 62 developed and developing countries. For our benchmark regression analysis, we employ the labor market regulation rigidity index developed by Campos et al. (2018), employing alternative indices constructed by Forteza and Rama (2006) and Botero et al. (2004) for robustness checks. Our unique measure of exchange rate volatility captures unpredictable fluctuations in the real exchange rate over the last three months. We used the fixed effects model, analogous to the triple-D estimation for the empirical analysis. We find negative and statistically significant impact of the interaction between exchange rate volatility and labor market rigidity on export growth. The findings indicate that in a country where labor market rigidity is one standard deviation higher, a one standard deviation increases in exchange rate volatility reduce export growth by 3.45 percentage points. The estimated coefficient is economically significant as well. This implies that the estimated coefficient reduces annual export growth by 3.45 percentage points relative to the annual average export growth of 3.2%. However, the estimated coefficient is smaller relative to the 40% standard deviation of annual average export growth. In subsample analysis, the results for developed and developing countries are consistent with the main findings.

title: Localized Fuel Taxes and Consumer Behavior: Spatial Relocation and the Price Elasticity of Fuel Demand
affiliations: University of Oxford - Center for Business Taxation and Universidad Nacional de Educacion a Distancia (UNED) - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Localized Fuel Taxes and Consumer Behavior: Spatial Relocation and the Price Elasticity of Fuel Demand
detail.abstract: In this paper, we examine how localized fuel taxes induce spatial relocation of purchases, and their implications for estimating the price elasticity of fuel demand. Our empirical approach exploits multiple regional fuel tax changes in Spain, combined with granular subregional data on fuel prices and purchases. First, we document substantial spatial relocation: near regional borders, the elasticity of diesel purchases with respect to cross-regional price differences is as large as -9. Second, we show that failing to account for such relocation leads to a pronounced upward bias in estimated fuel price elasticities. Specifications that ignore cross-regional purchases suggest highly elastic fuel demand, whereas accounting for relocation renders fuel demand inelastic. Our findings highlight the relevance of spatial relocation in the observed responses to localized fuel taxes, and suggest that localized environmental policies may be less effective in reducing CO2 emissions than previously assumed.

title: VAT Treatment of Commissionaire Arrangements in the European Union: A Practical Guide

detail.title: VAT Treatment of Commissionaire Arrangements in the European Union: A Practical Guide
detail.abstract: The commissionaire model is used widely in international trade. In such arrangements, an intermediary acts in its own name while representing another party, which leads the European Union VAT law to treat one commercial transaction as two separate supplies. While focusing primarily on supplies of goods, the article explains how Articles 14(2)(c) and 28 of the VAT Directive apply to commissionaire structures and examines the effects on domestic and international transactions. The article examines how Article 36a assigns transport in chain transactions and explains its interaction with triangulation rules. It also reviews structures involving non-EU principals and outlines the resulting VAT registration and compliance obligations. Using CJEU case law and practical examples, the article explains the correct VAT treatment of commissionaire transactions and the related compliance steps.

title: Tripolar Capital Dynamics as a Natural Tensor Realization of Prigogine's Dissipative Structures
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Tripolar Capital Dynamics as a Natural Tensor Realization of Prigogine's Dissipative Structures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. This research is conducted independently without any personal or financial relationships that could be perceived to influence the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a purely theoretical and mathematical study involving no human participants, patients, animals, or empirical data requiring ethical review.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted as part of the author's independent academic program on Two-State Mathematics and econophysics.

detail.abstract: Rooted in Prigogine's dissipative structure theory, this paper rigorously derives the tripolar capital dynamics equation as a natural mathematical closure of farfrom-equilibrium wealth evolution. We explicitly embed three irreducible dimensions into the individual-wealth Langevin stochastic differential equation: the Material Pole (capital stock inertia), the Energy Flow Pole (circulation velocity and kinetic dissipation), and the Information Structure Pole (institutional friction and social-consensus decay). Through Itô's lemma and the Kramers-Moyal expansion, we obtain the tripolar Fokker-Planck equation whose steady-state solution yields an analytic Pareto-tail exponent α = 1-2(µ M + ρ)/(σ 2 C + σ 2 Φ), revealing how information loss directly thickens wealth inequality. Moment closure then delivers the macroscopic tensor-coupled form: synchronizes with the wealth-thermalization phase transition. The results demonstrate that the tripolar structure is not an ad-hoc assumption but the unavoidable mathematical closure of dissipative-structure theory when applied to capital evolution. The framework unifies the series' prior findings-wealth thermalization, CRJ singularity, and critical slowing down-into a single dynamical equation, providing econophysics with a falsifiable, operationally grounded tensor theory of systemic risk. Paper Status: This is a working paper. Comments welcome.

title: 'The Financial Resources Curse' Hypothesis in Iraq: Application of ARDL and NARDL Models
affiliations: , University of Mazandaran (UMZ), University of Mazandaran (UMZ) and University of Mazandaran (UMZ)

detail.title: 'The Financial Resources Curse' Hypothesis in Iraq: Application of ARDL and NARDL Models
detail.abstract: In this study, we investigate the relationship between financial development and natural resource rents, examining the 'Financial Resource Curse' hypothesis. This examination is conducted separately for the banking system, the stock market, and the overall financial system in Iraq. The study covers the period from 1990 to 2021 and utilizes annual data sourced from the World Bank. Our analysis employs ARDL and NARDL models to estimate the relationships between these variables, and the DOLS estimator is used to ensure the robustness of the results. Our findings reveal a significant, negative, and statistically significant effect of resource rents on the development of Iraq's banking sector and its financial system as a whole. This outcome supports the 'Financial Resource Curse' hypothesis for these sectors in Iraq during the study period. However, the relationship between resource rents and the stock market development index is not statistically significant, making it difficult to draw conclusions regarding the existence of the financial resource curse in the stock market. Furthermore, improved institutional quality had a positive and statistically significant impact on financial development in both the banking and stock market sectors of Iraq during the study period. The Corruption Index also shows a positive and statistically significant long run effect on banking sector development, supporting the Grease the Wheels Hypothesis. However, it has a negative impact on the development of the stock market and the financial system.

title: Tax Simplicity vs. Firm Growth: Evidence from a Gross Receipts Taxation Regime
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Tax Simplicity vs. Firm Growth: Evidence from a Gross Receipts Taxation Regime
detail.abstract: This paper examines the effects of a gross receipt taxation (GRT) regime introduced in 2013 to simplify tax compliance for micro-firms. Using administrative firm-level data and a comprehensive empirical strategy, including interaction models, fuzzy regression discontinuity, two-way fixed effects, Heckman selection correction, propensity score matching, and heterogeneity analysis, the paper evaluates how GRT affected performance and firm growth. The paper finds that firms self-select into GRT based on the joint distribution of gross receipts and profit margins, consistent with a theoretical model of profit-maximizing behavior. Contrary to a mechanical response at the eligibility threshold, no discontinuity in entry or outcomes is detected, indicating that eligibility alone did not drive participation. Average treatment effects are small or misleading due to strong heterogeneity, with very small firms benefiting from GRT through reduced administrative costs and higher growth, while larger firms near the eligibility limit experienced lower performance and long-run growth. The findings imply that simplified tax regimes can successfully support micro-enterprise entry but may unintentionally discourage scaling if rigidly designed.

title: Micro Firms Under Gross Receipts Taxation: Regime Choice and Revenue Reporting
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Micro Firms Under Gross Receipts Taxation: Regime Choice and Revenue Reporting
detail.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical model of firm behavior under gross receipts taxation (GRT) in an environment where entrepreneurs can choose between a profit-based tax regime and a GRT regime subject to a statutory eligibility threshold. Firms produce both legally reported and illegally concealed income, face convex costs of production, and are subject to an exogenous probability of audit. When audited, firms incur a fine proportional to the magnitude of undeclared income, capturing the increasing marginal risk of evasion. The model characterizes optimal reporting behavior, regime choice, and output decisions across heterogeneous firms, and yields sharp predictions regarding tax evasion, formal profitability, and the incidence of zombie firms. These theoretical predictions are compared to descriptive patterns from the 2013 introduction of the GRT in Slovenia.

title: Part II -The Market Power Hierarchy Framework
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Part II -The Market Power Hierarchy Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal, financial, or professional relationships with any individuals, organizations, or institutions that could be perceived to have influenced the content of this work. This book is an independent and original analysis developed solely for educational and informational purposes. Any references to industries, market structures, or business practices are intended to illustrate economic concepts and do not reflect any affiliation or endorsement. detail.abstract:
The Hierarchy of Market Power introduces a structured framework for analyzing how firms gain, sustain, and exercise control within markets. Moving beyond traditional binary models of perfect competition and monopoly, this work conceptualizes market power as a continuum organized into five distinct levels, each defined by varying degrees of dominance, behavioral patterns, and economic outcomes.

The book examines how increasing market share alters firm incentives, shifting behavior from reactive competition to strategic control. It explores the mechanisms that enable firms to move up the hierarchy, including barriers to entry, economies of scale, network effects, and access to key resources. These factors not only limit competition but also reinforce the stability of dominant positions over time.

In addition, the framework connects market power to broader economic implications, including pricing dynamics, innovation, consumer welfare, and market efficiency. Through theoretical analysis and applied case studies, the book highlights how dominance can both drive progress and create risks of inefficiency, reduced competition, and concentrated control.

Special attention is given to the transformation of market power in the digital age, where platform-based models, data accumulation, and interconnected networks have introduced new forms of dominance. The work also addresses the challenges these developments pose for regulation and ethical governance.

By integrating theory with practical insight, The Hierarchy of Market Power provides a comprehensive approach to understanding how markets function, how power is distributed, and how it shapes economic outcomes in both traditional and modern contexts.

title: Of Equitable Liability

detail.title: Of Equitable Liability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationship to anyone who could have influenced his work. His work is his own.

detail.abstract: Limited liability is foundational to modern corporate finance because it permits diversified equity ownership, market liquidity, and impersonal capital formation. Yet finance models treat the shareholder liability cap as an exogenous legal boundary, not as a separately priced protection. This paper studies the pricing failure created by that convention. When corporate harm exceeds firm-side assets, insurance, indemnities, statutory funds, and bankruptcy-estate resources, the residual loss is not eliminated; it is shifted to involuntary creditors, tort claimants, workers, taxpayers, ecosystems, non-human sentient life, and future generations. Prior proposals, including unlimited shareholder liability, bonding, public charges, asset requirements, and mandatory firm-level insurance, address parts of the judgment-proofness problem but do not jointly provide holder-level incidence, transfer reset, dynamic underwriting, risk-based capital, run-off, reserve-backed compensation, secondary-market signalling, and no-insurance boundaries. The question is whether the capital-market benefits of limited liability can be preserved while eliminating the zero-price subsidy embedded in investor insulation from residual social loss. The paper argues that costless limited liability is economically analogous to a zero-premium legal put, or free excess-loss protection, written on residual harm. It proposes removing that subsidy by converting the shareholder liability shield into a renewable, holder-linked Limited Liability Certificate purchased from regulated underwriters at market-discovered premia. The mechanism, termed Equitable Liability, prices the residual layer (H − A)^+, where H is legally cognisable harm and A is firm-side loss-absorbing capacity.A benchmark model shows that actuarially fair certificate premia capitalise omitted residual harm into ownership. An equilibrium underwriting model derives premia from conditional expected residual loss, signal precision, risk-based capital, expected shortfall, adverse selection, moral-hazard covenants, and administrative loadings. The extended architecture formalises certified-equity valuation, portfolio-certificate choice, liability-premium beta, extraordinary repricing, certificate-market signals, securitised risk transfer, reinsurance, retrocession, claims-waterfall non-impairment, legacy-risk premia, no-cover discontinuities, and equity-premium death spirals. Equitable Liability reframes limited liability as a priced, renewable, claims-backed, and market-observable excess-loss protection rather than a free attribute of the share. It preserves tradable equity while making residual harm endogenous to valuation, expected returns, insurer capital allocation, and corporate risk management. More generally, the paper identifies the legal underpricing of shareholder insulation as a central distortion in capital allocation and proposes a market-consistent architecture for repricing that insulation through underwriting, solvency regulation, and claims-paying capacity. By making the shield conditional, renewable, and capital-backed, Equitable Liability supplies a mechanism for aligning capital allocation with ecosystems, animals, and future generations.

title: Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphone Sensors:,A Machine Learning Perspective
affiliations: Chitkara University, Chitkara University, Chitkara University and Chitkara University

detail.title: Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphone Sensors:,A Machine Learning Perspective
detail.abstract: Smartphones equipped with tri-axial accelerometers and gyroscopes enable,ubiquitous human activity recognition (HAR). This paper presents an,end-to-end designed HAR pipeline incorporating signal processing techniques,(Butterworth filters, gravity/body separation, 128-sample sliding windows),and systematic comparison of multiple machine learning architectures. We,design and evaluate five distinct models: Support Vector Machine (SVM),,Random Forest (RF), 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long,Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and a novel CNN-BiLSTM hybrid architecture.,To address class imbalance, SMOTE is applied with careful design parameter,selection (k=5 neighbors). The designed CNN-BiLSTM architecture achieves,the highest accuracy of 92.87% with F1-score of 0.9293. Additionally,,through optimization design, the 1D CNN model is reduced to 45 KB,TensorFlow Lite size (85.94% reduction from 320 KB) with only 0.4%,accuracy loss. Real-world deployment achieves 12 ms inference latency on,Snapdragon 778G with <0.3% battery consumption per hour, demonstrating,the effectiveness of designed hybrid deep learning architectures for,practical, resource-constrained edge computing scenarios. Results show,F1-scores across six activity classes (Walking, Upstairs, Downstairs,,Sitting, Standing, Lying) ranging from 0.8332 to 0.96, indicating robust,design across diverse activity types.
