detail.abstract: Certificate of Need (CON) laws require certain health care facilities to obtain permission from a state board before opening or expanding. Currently 27 states require hospitals to obtain a CON, 11 states apply CON only to certain non-hospital providers, and 12 states have no CON program. This paper aims to augment the currently available data, allowing researchers to study the effect of CON laws on more services or estimate the effect of policy changes. We provide a new database documenting which states applied CON laws to hospitals in each year since 1980.

title: How State Overreach Drives Technological Innovation as a Form of Political Resistance: Toward a Framework for the Properties of Conscious Mass
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: How State Overreach Drives Technological Innovation as a Form of Political Resistance: Toward a Framework for the Properties of Conscious Mass
detail.abstract: This paper asks: does institutional overreach systematically produce counter-technologies and counter-institutions whose architecture corresponds inversely and proportionally to the specific failure modes of the collapse that produced them? Drawing on three historical case studies, the Gutenberg printing press, Soviet Samizdat, and Bitcoin, the paper argues that the answer is yes, and that this pattern is structural rather than contingent. The paper identifies stupefaction, the systematic degradation of civic and epistemic capacity in the governed population, as the operational precondition for elite capture rather than its incidental byproduct, and proposes a first formal mapping of qualitative institutional variables onto physical analogs through a weighted matrix. The 1 RESISTANCE INNOVATION CYCLES framework engages and extends existing literature on contentious politics, institutional path dependency, punctuated equilibrium, and the politics of artifacts. It is presented as a theoretical foundation and an invitation to empirical testing rather than a completed formalization.

title: Graph theory-coupled genetic algorithm optimization of piping networks for temperature uniformity in multi-stack SOFC systems
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology and Huazhong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Graph theory-coupled genetic algorithm optimization of piping networks for temperature uniformity in multi-stack SOFC systems
detail.abstract: Multi-stack solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) systems are increasingly deployed for distributed energy systems, where temperature uniformity among stacks is critical for ensuring operational stability. However, multi-stack systems involve complex hierarchical piping networks, and flow distribution among stacks strongly influences heat generation uniformity, thereby directly impacting system temperature uniformity. To improve system temperature uniformity, this study proposes an optimization framework that couples a graph-theory-based hydraulic model with a genetic algorithm to systematically design piping networks. Pipe length, diameter, and valve opening are selected as design variables, and the minimization of the stack temperature uniformity index (UTD) is set as the optimization objective. For an example 35-stack system, the optimized design reduces the UTD from 30.36 to 10.67, a reduction of 64.9%. Further analyses of stoichiometric ratio, current density, stack number, and stack arrangement pattern indicate that increasing the stoichiometric ratio and stack count moderately degrades temperature uniformity, whereas uniform stack arrangements substantially outperform non-uniform descending configurations. The proposed framework provides an efficient and scalable methodology for the thermal management design of large-scale multi-stack SOFC systems.

title: Regional Multi-Well Groundwater Level Forecasting under Irregular Monitoring Layouts Using a GCN-LSTM Framework
affiliations: Sichuan University, Sichuan University, Sichuan University and Sichuan University

detail.title: Regional Multi-Well Groundwater Level Forecasting under Irregular Monitoring Layouts Using a GCN-LSTM Framework
detail.abstract: Accurate groundwater level forecasting is essential for groundwater monitoring, risk assessment, and sustainable water resource management in rapidly urbanizing regions. This study proposes a graph-based spatiotemporal forecasting framework for regional multi-well groundwater level prediction using a Graph Convolutional Network–Long Short-Term Memory (GCN–LSTM) model. Daily monitoring data from 56 state-owned observation wells in Chengdu, China, collected from 2019 to 2023, are used to construct a graph that represents inter-well spatial relationships under an irregular monitoring layout. In the proposed framework, the GCN component captures spatial dependence and heterogeneous interactions among wells, while the LSTM component models temporal evolution in groundwater level fluctuations. Two data-availability scenarios are further considered to reflect practical monitoring conditions: a groundwater-level-only setting and a multi-factor setting incorporating rainfall and water temperature. Results show that the proposed framework can achieve accurate multi-step forecasting for multiple wells simultaneously under both scenarios, while the inclusion of additional temporal drivers further improves the prediction of fluctuation trends and turning points. The results also indicate that explicitly modeling inter-well spatial relationships is beneficial for regional groundwater forecasting in heterogeneous urban environments. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective and transferable approach for groundwater level prediction in irregular monitoring networks and has practical implications for urban groundwater management and early warning.

title: Will Mine Closures Trigger Low-Flow Crises in River Systems? Insights from a Machine Learning Approach for the Vistula Basin, Poland
affiliations: AGH University  of Science and Technology, AGH University of Krakow, AGH University of Krakow, Institute of Meteorology and Water Management and Institute of Meteorology and Water Management

detail.title: Will Mine Closures Trigger Low-Flow Crises in River Systems? Insights from a Machine Learning Approach for the Vistula Basin, Poland
detail.abstract: Coal mine closures represent a major anthropogenic shift in regional hydrology, as long-term mine dewatering has become an integral component of river flow regimes. This study assesses how the planned phase-out of mine drainage in the Upper Silesian Coal Basin (2020–2049) may interact with climate change to reshape streamflow dynamics in the Upper Vistula River system, with a focus on the Przemsza–Vistula corridor. Future streamflows were simulated using the SWAT model within the CHASE-PL framework, driven by nine bias-corrected EURO-CORDEX climate projections under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios. To improve predictive robustness, a machine-learning–based Conditional Weighted Regression (CWR) approach was applied to dynamically combine ensemble outputs into a Weighted Ensemble Streamflow (WES) projection. The hydrological impact of mine closures was quantified by removing water discharges according to the closure schedule. Results indicate that mine closure primarily affects low-flow conditions. In the Przemsza River system, the probability of flows below the historical 10th percentile increases markedly after closure. Monthly reductions in the 10th percentile for flows may reach up to 4.5 m³/s (~35%) in the Przemsza River and up to 1.4 m³/s (~15%) in the Vistula River. Seasonal patterns show increased flows in spring–summer, and decreased flows in autumn, reflecting combined climatic and anthropogenic effects. The study demonstrates that hybrid SWAT–machine learning frameworks enhance climate impact assessments and provide a robust tool for evaluating hydrological consequences of large-scale socio-economic transitions such as mine closures.

title: HBCM: A Multi-Scale Framework for Connection-Level Inference of Brain Structure–Function Coupling
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences and Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Wuhan Institute of Physics and Mathematics

detail.title: HBCM: A Multi-Scale Framework for Connection-Level Inference of Brain Structure–Function Coupling
detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Understanding how white-matter anatomy shapes functional brain dynamics is a fundamental question in systems neuroscience and a prerequisite for principled analysis of multimodal neuroimaging data. Existing approaches typically treat all connections uniformly, assume linear or simple parametric relationships, or overlook the hierarchical organization of the brain, making it diﬃcult to distinguish genuinely coupled connections from noise or to quantify individual diﬀerences in a statistically rigorous way. This work develops a uniﬁed probabilistic framework for connection-level inference of structure–function coupling in multimodal brain connectivity data. ​Methods: We propose a hierarchical Bayesian coupling model that integrates three methodological components within a single generative model: spike-and-slab mixture priors for automatic, threshold-free connection selection; network-speciﬁc Gaussian processes with Matérn covariance for nonparametric modeling of nonlinear structure– function relationships; and a three-level hierarchical decomposition that separates network-pair, connection-speciﬁc, and subject-speciﬁc contributions to coupling variability. Posterior inference is performed via Gibbs sampling with Pólya–Gamma data augmentation, which yields conjugate updates for the logistic mixture component and avoids Metropolis–Hastings steps prone to poor mixing. Results: On synthetic data spanning six signal-to-noise levels and six functional forms, the model achieves greater than 90% sensitivity while maintaining false discovery rates below 9% across all conditions. Biophysical simulations using neural mass models conﬁrm accurate recovery of coupling patterns from mechanistic neural dynamics. Application to multimodal neuroimaging data from 136 healthy young adults reveals systematic spatial organization consistent with cortical hierarchy, with primary sensory-motor regions exhibiting strong coupling and transmodal association cortex exhibiting weaker correspondence; meta-analytic cognitive decoding further aligns the recovered coupling gradient with a sensorimotor-to-transmodal functional axis. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides a uniﬁed, principled approach for connection-level structure– function coupling inference, jointly addressing connection selection, nonlinearity, and hierarchical variability. An open-source implementation accompanies this work to support reproducibility and extension.

title: Corporate Sustainable Bonds in Brazil: Market Reactions and Spillover Effects
affiliations: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN), Federal University at Rio Grande do Norte - UFRN and Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN)

detail.title: Corporate Sustainable Bonds in Brazil: Market Reactions and Spillover Effects
detail.abstract: This study investigates the Brazilian capital market's reaction to sustainable bond issuances by publicly traded companies on B3. Using event study methodology on 62 issuances between 2015 and 2024, we measure cumulative abnormal returns across multiple temporal windows. Results reveal a systematic pattern of negative abnormal returns, with an average cumulative abnormal return of -1.71% over 21 trading days, significant at the 5% level, contrasting with evidence from developed markets, where green bond issuances typically generate positive or neutral returns. Spillover analysis on 248 competing firm observations identifies no significant impacts, suggesting the market treats these issuances as idiosyncratic decisions. Sub-period analysis indicates possible deterioration in market perception after 2020. Findings carry implications for issuers, investors, and regulators. This study contributes to sustainable finance literature by documenting the first systematic evidence on green

title: ChamferCAD: A Two-Stage Graph Learning Framework with Statistical Feature Enhancement for Automated Chamfer Defeaturing
affiliations: Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University and Zhejiang University

detail.title: ChamferCAD: A Two-Stage Graph Learning Framework with Statistical Feature Enhancement for Automated Chamfer Defeaturing
detail.abstract: Automated defeaturing of boundary-representation (B-Rep) CAD models is a key preprocessing step for analysis-oriented simplification, yet transition features remain difficult because their removability depends on surrounding topology. Most learning-based B-Rep methods formulate defeaturing as face-level recognition: they identify chamfer faces but do not decide whether the corresponding connected feature chain can be suppressed while preserving a valid solid. This paper addresses this gap with a two-stage graph-learning framework for chamfer defeaturing and the ChamferCAD benchmark suite. The benchmark includes a basic subset with sparse uniform chamfers and a harder ChamferCAD++ subset with connected, variable-width, and asymmetric chamfer chains; both subsets provide face-level recognition labels, and ChamferCAD++ further provides chain-level cleanup-feasibility labels. The Chamfer Recognition Network (CRN) first localizes chamfer faces on an attributed face-adjacency graph. The predicted faces are then grouped into candidate chains, and the Cleanup Decision Network (CDN) estimates cleanability by fusing pooled graph embeddings, neighbor-angle statistics, and prediction-confidence statistics. Experiments show that, on the basic ChamferCAD subset, CRN reaches 99.30% accuracy and 99.28% F1-score with only 0.03M parameters, remaining within 0.20 accuracy points and 0.25 F1-score points of AAGNet while using about 12.3× fewer parameters. On the harder ChamferCAD++ subset, CRN achieves the best performance among the evaluated methods, with 97.83% accuracy, 97.82% precision, 97.83% recall, and 97.82% F1-score. CDN reaches 92.39% accuracy for chain-level cleanup decision. Ablations show that dihedral angle and face width dominate recognition, whereas neighbor-angle statistics provide the principal evidence for cleanability. The results indicate that CAD defeaturing should evaluate both feature identity and geometric actionability.

title: A Hybrid Multi-Stage Pipeline for Restoring Damaged and Occluded Old Photographs
affiliations: University of Anbar

detail.title: A Hybrid Multi-Stage Pipeline for Restoring Damaged and Occluded Old Photographs
detail.abstract: Restoring old and damaged photographs is a challenging problem in computational photography, complicated by the simultaneous presence of structured degradations such as scratches, blotches, fading, and missing content regions. Existing single-model approaches address only one degradation type at a time, while current multi-stage pipelines typically rely on manually annotated damage masks and a single fixed set of pretrained inpainting weights, limiting their scalability and restoration quality on heterogeneous photo collections. In this paper, we propose a five-stage hybrid restoration pipeline integrating BOPBL, SAM2, AOT-GAN, GFPGAN v1.3, and DeOldify under a unified framework with three novel contributions. First, we introduce a Boundary-Aware Adaptive Dilation (BAAD) module that refines SAM2-generated damage masks based on local boundary characteristics, replacing the fixed-kernel dilation used in conventional pipelines. Second, we propose an Automatic Adaptive Weight Selection (AAWS) mechanism that dynamically selects AOT-GAN pretrained weights between CelebA-HQ and Places2 based on detected image content, eliminating manual weight configuration. Third, we demonstrate through controlled experiments that placing facial enhancement (GFPGAN) before colorization (DeOldify) yields perceptually superior results compared to the reverse order. The proposed pipeline is evaluated on a curated dataset spanning three damage severity levels drawn from CelebA-HQ, Places2, and the BOPBL real-old-photographs benchmark. Compared to the AOT-GAN baseline, our method achieves PSNR improvements of up to +7.97 dB and LPIPS reductions of 54% under light damage conditions, with consistent gains across all severity levels. The pipeline requires minimal user interaction: Stage 2 (SAM2) operates in prompted mode, where the user provides click prompts on visually apparent damaged regions to generate the initial segmentation mask. All subsequent stages — BAAD refinement, AOT-GAN inpainting, GFPGAN enhancement, and DeOldify colorization — execute fully automatically without further intervention,K

title: Can Judicial Deterrence Curb Corporate ”Say-Do Discrepancies”? —A Quasi-Natural Experiment from the Environmental Courts
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Macau University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Can Judicial Deterrence Curb Corporate ”Say-Do Discrepancies”? —A Quasi-Natural Experiment from the Environmental Courts
detail.abstract: Against the backdrop of global green development and China’s sustainable economic transition, many firms exaggerate green-transition disclosures to cater to national strategies and capital market preferences, leading to a severe "Say–Do Gap". Based on signaling theory, this study uses the phased establishment of environmental courts in 208 prefecture-level cities as a quasi-natural experiment, adopting a staggered DID design with 2007–2023 panel data of Chinese A-share listed firms for empirical tests. Results show widespread corporate green pandering, with improved disclosure not translating into actual carbon reduction. Environmental courts effectively curb this behavior, with environmental litigation risk as the core mediating channel. Heterogeneity tests reveal stronger deterrence in regions with weaker regulation/heavier pollution and polluting firms with stronger environmental technology. This study enriches literature from a judicial deterrence perspective and provides implications for substantive corporate green transition.

title: The asymmetric moderating effect of AI empowerment on public service mismatch and subjective well-being: Evidence from China’s frontier regions
affiliations: China University of Political Science and Law, Beibu Gulf University and Beijing Technology and Business University

detail.title: The asymmetric moderating effect of AI empowerment on public service mismatch and subjective well-being: Evidence from China’s frontier regions
detail.abstract: This paper studies the effect of public service mismatch on subjective well-being for small-sized regions of China, highlighting the asymmetric moderating role of AI empowerment. We analyzed 5,440 micro-observations from China’s frontier regions using an instrumental variable (IV-2SLS) to dissect public resource deficits into physical infrastructure and soft social service mismatch. We demonstrated that relative deprivation locus has turned towards developmental constraints, while soft service deficits inflict a significant toll on the wellbeing of individuals by both eroding vertical political trust and horizontal social integration. Notably, AI empowerment reveals an asymmetric “double-edged sword” effect. AI is a digital compensator that reduces psychological isolation caused by physical infrastructure constraints, but AI is an expectation gap amplifier that can deteriorate social capital if local soft services are not adequate. Our results challenge the linear digital dividend hypothesis, which suggests that technology exacerbates structural alienation if not matched with offline human-capital investments, providing insights for digital governance and spatial justice.

title: Corporate Payout Policy and Bad-News Hoarding
affiliations: Athens University of Economics and Business - Department of Business Administration, Athens University of Economics and Business, University of Zurich - Department Finance and Athens University of Economics and Business - Department of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: Corporate Payout Policy and Bad-News Hoarding
detail.abstract: We investigate how G7-listed firms (2000–2023) adjust payout policies when facing stock price crash risk, which proxies for investor concerns about bad-news hoarding. Exposed firms increase dividends and repurchases to reassure investors, shifting their payout mix toward dividends given their stronger commitment value. However, these stabilizing payouts entail real economic costs: under high crash risk, firms, especially smaller ones, fund payouts by cutting CAPEX and R&D. Driven by an agency/free-cash-flow channel, these commitments discipline liquidity and signal confidence. Ultimately, payout policy serves as a vital tool to manage crash risk, albeit at the expense of long-term investment.

title: Two-Stage AI Adoption in Technology-Taker Economies: Platform Capture, Infrastructure, and Firm Constraints in Latin America
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Two-Stage AI Adoption in Technology-Taker Economies: Platform Capture, Infrastructure, and Firm Constraints in Latin America
detail.abstract: Consumer-side generative AI encounter in Latin America is shaped by institutional and infrastructural channels specific to technology-taker economies, but not those the standard political-economy literature predicts. This paper develops a two-stage framework, distinguishing consumer-encounter from firm-expectation, with distinct binding constraints at each stage. Stage-1 analysis draws on a weekly Google Trends panel of generative AI search interest across seven platforms for nineteen Latin American countries (2020–2024), cross-validated against Cloudflare Radar and Similarweb. One robust finding emerges: the combination of political stability with weak state capacity predicts Gemini's market share through an ecosystem-default mechanism concentrated in low-formal-sector, thinly engaged consumer markets (joint institutional F(3,12) = 5.21, p = 0.016; robust to bootstrap inference and outlier exclusion). Two additional patterns — internet penetration individually predicting encounter velocity (standardized β = 0.66, p = 0.099) and regulatory quality individually correlating with platform diversification — are suggestive individual-coefficient findings not clearing joint-family significance. Stage-2 analysis draws on employer-expectation data from the WEF Future of Jobs 2025 survey for Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, and Mexico, revealing that firm-side constraints are operational-regulatory and human-capital rather than macro-institutional. Each stage falls outside the scope of the standard institutions-and-investment literature in a different way: the real-options mechanism requires irreversible commitment under political uncertainty, a condition consumer-side adoption of zero-marginal-cost products does not satisfy and firm-side adoption satisfies only partially. The paper develops evidence consistent with a scope limitation on the institutions-and-investment literature.

title: The Weapon Itself is the Threat: Nuclear Weapons, the Knowledge Problem, and Normal Accidents
affiliations: and

detail.title: The Weapon Itself is the Threat: Nuclear Weapons, the Knowledge Problem, and Normal Accidents
detail.abstract: This paper argues that the primary danger of nuclear deterrence arises not from leaders acting irrationally, but from inherent limitations of complex systems operating under epistemic constraints. We integrate the work of Don Lavoie's analysis of the knowledge problem with Charles Perrow's theory of normal accidents to explain why nuclear command-and-control systems are unreliable. Lavoie shows that centralized authorities cannot access dispersed tacit knowledge, while Perrow shows that tightly coupled, complex systems are prone to cascading failures. Together, these mechanisms suggest that even if deterrence works as intended, its implementation is structurally fragile and dangerous. We illustrate these theoretical insights through six historical cases involving near accidents, which show that outcomes depend not on system reliability, but on context-specific judgment, deviations from protocol, and good fortune.

title: Tax Robots? Evaluating the Economic and Social Implications of Automation Levies
affiliations: University of Colorado at Denver - Department of Finance and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Tax Robots? Evaluating the Economic and Social Implications of Automation Levies
detail.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) and robotics increasingly perform tasks traditionally held by human workers, the debate over "robot taxation" has moved from theoretical speculation to a central pillar of fiscal policy discussion. Proponents argue that taxing robots can mitigate rising wealth inequality and fund the transition for displaced workers, while critics contend such levies stifle innovation and reduce national competitiveness. This paper analyzes the trade-offs between fiscal stability and technological progress, proposing a framework for an "automation-neutral" tax system that shifts the burden from labor to capital without halting the march of productivity.

detail.abstract: Cryptocurrencies are five times more volatile than stocks-why? We shed light on this issue by applying a variance decomposition that separates noise and different forms of information in return. We find that noise plays the dominant role in the price variance, accounting for 48.74%. The remaining variance is distributed across information types: 14.85% from market-wide information, 15.41% from private information, and 20.82% from public information. Over time, the share of noise declines while the market-wide component increases, suggesting that the cryptocurrency market is maturing as it becomes more integrated into the traditional financial system and gains broader institutional adoption. We also find that the noise share in cryptocurrencies is significantly higher than in traditional assets such as stocks (22.55%), fiat currencies (18.31%), and commodities (14.93%). Additionally, we show that the leverage effect in crypto is similar to the commodity market, where prices positively correlate with both volatility and noise and the high noise level in cryptocurrencies is closely linked to the strong participation of noise investors.

title: A Lofty Concept to Outmode the Strait of Hormuz in the Global Petroleum Architecture
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Lofty Concept to Outmode the Strait of Hormuz in the Global Petroleum Architecture

keywords: First Mile / Last Mile -The Lighterer Revolution

detail.abstract: Global petroleum logistics remain dangerously dependent on the Strait of Hormuz, a single maritime chokepoint whose disruption would trigger immediate and far‑reaching economic consequences. Despite decades of analysis, most proposed alternatives replicate the same structural vulnerabilities: centralized routes, maritime bottlenecks, and infrastructure that cannot adapt to geopolitical volatility. This paper re‑examines the underlying assumptions of the current petroleum architecture and evaluates whether a fundamentally different logistical model could reduce or eliminate chokepoint exposure. By reassessing barrel‑per‑mile economics, first‑mile and last‑mile constraints, and the strategic fragility of existing transport corridors, the paper explores whether a viable, scalable alternative now exists where none was previously feasible.

title: The Robot Tax Debate: Economic and Social Implications of Automation Levies
affiliations: University of Colorado at Denver - Department of Finance and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Robot Tax Debate: Economic and Social Implications of Automation Levies
detail.abstract: Rapid advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and robotics are transforming labor markets and challenging traditional tax systems built around human employment. As automation increasingly substitutes for labor, policymakers face growing concerns regarding declining labor-tax revenues, rising income inequality, and the economic displacement of workers. At the center of this debate is the proposal of "robot taxes," where firms adopting automation technologies may face additional taxation to offset social and fiscal costs. This paper examines the economic rationale for automation levies and evaluates their potential consequences for innovation, productivity, and long-run competitiveness. While supporters argue that robot taxation could provide resources for worker retraining and social adjustment, opponents warn that excessive taxation may discourage technological progress and slow economic growth. We propose an automation-neutral fiscal framework that gradually shifts taxation away from labor income and toward broader capital-based mechanisms while preserving incentives for innovation and productivity expansion. .

title: El Principio de Reciprocidad Institucional

detail.title: El Principio de Reciprocidad Institucional

detail.abstract:
This work argues that the central problem in recent reforms to the right to strike does not lie in the possibility of establishing restrictions—permitted under international law in specific circumstances—but in the absence of proportional compensatory mechanisms accompanying such limitations.

Through the analysis of the legal regime applicable to police officers and penitentiary personnel, the study identifies a particularly intense configuration of restrictions on collective labor rights. These sectors are often simultaneously deprived of the right to strike, full trade unionization, effective collective bargaining, and impartial mechanisms for resolving labor disputes.

To describe this situation, the study introduces the category of “restriction without representation”, referring to institutional arrangements in which limitations on the right to strike are not accompanied by substitute institutions capable of guaranteeing labor representation. Under such conditions, the restriction ceases to constitute a legitimate regulation of the right and instead becomes an impairment of its essential content, placing it in tension with the constitutional and international labor rights framework.

Based on a comparative analysis of regulatory models in Uruguay, Brazil, Chile, and Canada, the work demonstrates that the legitimacy of restrictions on the right to strike depends on the existence of equivalent compensatory mechanisms. The sufficiency of these mechanisms can be assessed through a structural proportionality test.

On this basis, the study examines the constitutional and conventional tensions raised by the Argentine reform of 2026, proposes a categorical distinction between armed forces, federal security forces, and provincial police, and introduces the notion of “preventive neutralization of conflict” as a critical concept to describe policies that restrict collective conflict without establishing substitute institutions capable of guaranteeing labor representation.

Within this framework, the work formulates the Institutional Reciprocity Principle, according to which any intense restriction of a collective right requires the existence of equivalent institutional mechanisms that preserve the effective capacity for labor representation and dispute resolution.

The study contributes to contemporary constitutional debate by proposing this analytical principle as a criterion for evaluating the legitimacy of strong restrictions on collective rights within public employment.

title: Dan VĂTĂMAN * THE 2024 EUROPEAN ELECTIONS: OUTCOMES AND IMPLICATIONS FOR THE RENEWAL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION INSTITUTIONAL LEADERSHIP

detail.title: Dan VĂTĂMAN * THE 2024 EUROPEAN ELECTIONS: OUTCOMES AND IMPLICATIONS FOR THE RENEWAL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION INSTITUTIONAL LEADERSHIP
detail.abstract: As enshrined in the treaties on which the European Union (EU) is founded, citizens are directly represented at Union level in the European Parliament, an institution that plays a key role in appointing the European Commission and other EU bodies and institutions. Member States are represented in the European Council by their Heads of State or Government and in the Council by their governments, themselves democratically accountable either to their national Parliaments, or to their citizens. In the light of the treaties provisions and taking into account the strong interest of EU citizens in the 2024 European elections and awareness of their significance for the future of Union, the purpose of this study is to describe the process of renewing the EU institutional leadership, with emphasis on the steps to be taken by the end of 2024. In this approach, the analysis will be focused first of all on the aspects related to constitution of the political groups and constituent plenary sitting of the new European Parliament. As is expected, further analysis will deepen the aspects related to election of the European Commission President and appointment of the new College of Commissioners. Also, will be addressed issues related to the election of the new President of the European Council, the Parliament vote on investiture of Commission and election of the European Ombudsman.

title: AlphaGlass: Interpretable Portfolios for Flexible Investment Objectives
affiliations: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology - Department of Economics and Management, University of California, Berkeley, University of California - Haas School of Business and Karlsruhe Institute of Technology - Department of Economics and Management

detail.title: AlphaGlass: Interpretable Portfolios for Flexible Investment Objectives
detail.abstract: We propose AlphaGlass, an inherently interpretable machine-learning framework for constructing portfolios that directly optimize investment objectives. AlphaGlass maps stock characteristics into additive signals with sparse interactions and converts these signals into long-short portfolios through a differentiable rankand-mask layer. This end-to-end design allows the model to optimize objectives such as the Sharpe ratio or mean-variance utility while keeping portfolio weights interpretable and traceable to specific characteristics and interactions. We show theoretically that in-sample objective maximization consistently estimates the population objective and that the differentiable rank-and-mask layer is a faithful smooth proxy for the corresponding conventional long-short quantile portfolio. In U.S. equities, AlphaGlass delivers strong out-of-sample performance and reveals economically interpretable drivers of long and short positions.

title: Rationalizable Incentives: Interim Rationalizable Implementation of Correspondences
affiliations: , University of Cincinnati - Department of Economics and Brown University

detail.title: Rationalizable Incentives: Interim Rationalizable Implementation of Correspondences
detail.abstract: Are there ways to enforce incentives free of equilibrium considerations? When the normative goals for a set of agents can be summarized in a set-valued rule and agents take actions that are rationalizable, a new theory of incentives emerges in which standard Bayesian incentive compatibility (BIC) is relaxed significantly. The paper studies the interim rationalizable implementation of social choice sets with a Cartesian product structure, a leading example thereof being ex-post efficiency. Setwise incentive compatibility (setwise IC), much weaker than BIC, is shown to be necessary for implementation. Setwise IC enforces incentives flexibly within the entire correspondence, instead of the pointwise enforcement entailed by BIC. Sufficient conditions, while based on the existence of SCFs in the correspondence that make truthful revelation a dominant strategy, are shown to be permissive to allow the implementation of ex-post efficiency in many settings where equilibrium implementation fails (e.g., bilateral trading, multidimensional signals). Furthermore, this success comes at little cost: all our mechanisms are well behaved, in the sense that best responses always exist.

title: DAN VATAMAN - THE EUROPEAN UNION'S EXTERNAL ACTION: NORMATIVE DEVELOPMENTS, CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES IN THE CURRENT INTERNATIONAL CONTEXT

detail.abstract: In view of recent developments in international relations, marked by strategic competition for supremacy, growing global instability and attempts to undermine the rules-based international order, this study aims to highlight the efforts made by the European Union to address these unprecedented challenges, focusing primarily on the reform elements and innovations introduced by the Lisbon Treaty aimed at increasing the coherence, impact and visibility of the European Union's external action. Once the legal basis for external action has been clarified, the focus will be on highlighting the European Union's priorities and strategic orientations, in particular the determination to strengthen its role as a global actor in the new multipolar geopolitical context.

title: Under the Radar: Selective Supply Chain Disclosure and Geopolitical Risk
affiliations: , The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School

detail.title: Under the Radar: Selective Supply Chain Disclosure and Geopolitical Risk
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether firms strategically manage the disclosure of global supply chain relationships in response to geopolitical risk. Using relationship-level supply chain data, we find that U.S. public firms are less likely to voluntarily disclose suppliers located in countries with higher geopolitical risk. This relation is stronger when disclosure may impose greater political or economic costs, and weaker when suppliers are more visible. We further show that disclosed supplier geopolitical risk is associated with higher short-run stock return volatility, whereas undisclosed supplier geopolitical risk is not, suggesting that selective disclosure delays the market’s incorporation of supply chain geopolitical exposure. Finally, undisclosed high-risk supplier relationships are more likely to be terminated in subsequent years, consistent with selective disclosure preceding real operational adjustments. Overall, our findings highlight selective disclosure as an important channel through which firms manage the visibility of geopolitical risk in global supply chains.

title: Belief Bias, Source Preference, and Preference for Robo-Advisor
affiliations: , Shenzhen University WeBank Institute of Fintech and The Hang Seng University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Belief Bias, Source Preference, and Preference for Robo-Advisor
detail.abstract: This paper investigates preferences for human versus robo-advisors using a dynamic source preference framework that allows for belief bias. We use a two-part experiment in which advice is generated by real-life investors and ChatGPT, and subjects value advice before and after learning advisors' objective accuracy. This design enables a dynamic decomposition of belief bias from taste-based source preference. Before disclosure, subjects are more likely to prefer robo-advice over human advice. After learning that the two advisors perform similarly, many subjects revise their valuations away from the robo-advisor and toward the human advisor, indicating that initial robo-preference partly reflects biased beliefs about algorithmic competence. Yet a substantial subset continues to prefer the robo-advisor after disclosure, revealing source preference independent of performance. Parametric estimates further show that taste-based source preference for the robo-advisor is more prevalent than for the human advisor. The results show that belief bias and taste-based source preference jointly shape demand for robo-advice, and that static measures may miss these distinct mechanisms.

title: On the Possibility of Informationally Inefficient Markets Without Noise

detail.title: On the Possibility of Informationally Inefficient Markets Without Noise
detail.abstract: Noise traders can be dispensed with entirely. Partial revelation of information through prices arises under any non-exponential expectedutility preference-including CRRA-without noise traders, random endowments, supply shocks, hedging motives, or behavioural biases. The model contains zero exogenous noise. The mechanism is a mismatch between the space in which market clearing aggregates signals and the Bayesian sufficient statistic. CARA demand is linear in log-odds, so prices aggregate in log-odds space and reveal the statistic exactly. Every other preference aggregates differently; the resulting Jensen gap makes revelation partial. I prove CARA is the unique fully revealing preference class, characterise the rational-expectations equilibrium via a contour-integration fixed point, and verify that partial revelation survives learning from prices. The Grossman-Stiglitz paradox is resolved: information acquisition has positive value within the rational class.

title: Bipartisan Corporatism: A Structural Interpretation of Policy Convergence
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Bipartisan Corporatism: A Structural Interpretation of Policy Convergence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Totally unfunded, independent research

detail.abstract:
This paper develops a structural framework for understanding policy convergence across major political parties in competitive democratic systems. It introduces the concept of bipartisan corporatism, defined as a condition in which electoral competition persists, but policy formation converges around frameworks compatible with large, organised economic interests.
Drawing on agenda-setting theory, institutional path dependence, and punctuated equilibrium models, the paper identifies a layered selection environment in which policy ideas are filtered prior to parliamentary deliberation. Within this environment, organised economic actors exert more consistent influence than diffuse voter interests due to differences in coordination, continuity, and access.
The paper further introduces two mechanisms: the policy filter, which systematically favours market-expanding policies over those that impose direct liability on established industries; and justification lock, through which repeated policy rationales become normalised, increasing the burden of proof for alternatives while reducing scrutiny of existing frameworks.
The result is a system characterised by visible political contestation alongside a structurally constrained policy space. Changes in governing party shift emphasis within this space but do not substantially alter its boundaries.
The framework explains both the persistence of policy convergence and the tendency for periods of divergence to be temporary and reabsorbed into existing institutional structures. It provides a basis for analysing how policy systems maintain stability while limiting the range of viable alternatives.

detail.abstract: Pakistan's economic trajectory is defined by a structural trap: stabilization followed by consumption-led expansion that inevitably triggers a balance of payments crisis, renewed borrowing, and deepened fiscal vulnerability. This paper proposes a comprehensive 20-year transition strategy to break this cycle by replacing debt-financed consumption with an investment-led, export-oriented model grounded in the principles of riba-free finance. The framework synthesizes the disciplined interventionist state model of 1960s South Korea with the decentralized, borderless opportunities of the 21st-century digital economy through a Dual-Track Growth Engine covering both physical industrialization and virtual services expansion. The strategy further proposes a Digital Public Infrastructure architecture centered on the Raast payment system and blockchain-enabled supply chain transparency to formalize Pakistan's shadow economy, estimated at over $450 billion. On the financing side, the paper develops an equity-based paradigm for mobilizing diaspora capital through Mudarabah-based instruments, replacing domestic sovereign debt with Sukuk and Ijarah certificates, and executing structured debt-for-equity swaps with bilateral creditors including China. A phased 20-year roadmap is provided, with mathematical risk assessment through the Contingent Claims Approach, and a candid treatment of academic critiques including IMF framework conflicts and principal-agent problems in equity-based financing. The objective is economic self-sufficiency by Pakistan's centenary in 2047.

title: Digital Ownership: The Tokenization of Real-World Assets
affiliations: McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management and

detail.title: Digital Ownership: The Tokenization of Real-World Assets
detail.abstract: We study conditions under which tokenization creates value for indivisible realworld assets (RWAs). We show that tokenization does not create value merely by making an asset transferable, fractional, or digitally scarce. Value arises only when digital ownership records change the economics of ownership by leveraging on asset characteristics and past ownership records on the blockchain. This may generate retained value for past owners, create provenance value for later buyers, separate usage and financial rights, support membership benefits through fractional ownership, or strengthen post-sale incentives through royalties. These forces determine whether tokenized markets are inactive, thin but informative, lemons-like, or liquid but uninformative. We discuss implications for art and luxury tokens, private-equity and venture-capital tokens, real-estate tokens, tokenized claims on a social enterprise, and sustainable-firm tokens.

title: Do Order-Book States Predict Passive-Buy Toxicity? Evidence from BTC Perpetual Futures

detail.title: Do Order-Book States Predict Passive-Buy Toxicity? Evidence from BTC Perpetual Futures
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether economically interpretable local order-book conditions predict short-horizon future returns and passive-buy adverse-selection risk in BTC perpetual futures. Using Binance Level 2 order-book snapshots merged with aggregate trade records, I construct a reduced-form empirical framework that summarizes local market conditions through recent directional order flow, near-touch bid-side absorption capacity, and liquidity-state fragility. The empirical design is motivated by a simple game-theoretic view of the limit order book: passive liquidity providers strategically supply or withdraw near-touch liquidity, while aggressive traders impose directional pressure that may or may not be absorbed depending on local displayed support. The main empirical result is that a flow-adjusted bid-absorption proxy is substantially more informative than raw directional flow alone. Across pooled regressions, horizon-robustness exercises, and day-by-day subsamples, higher recent sell pressure relative to best-bid depth predicts lower short-horizon future returns and higher passive-buy adverse-selection risk. Recent order-flow imbalance also contains predictive information, but the signal is weaker and less stable than the composite pressure-versus-capacity measure. In addition, liquidity fragility matters as a local state variable, indicating that execution risk depends not only on recent aggressive flow, but also on the vulnerability of the surrounding displayed liquidity. Taken together, the results suggest that passive-buy toxicity in crypto futures is best understood as a local imbalance between aggressive pressure and near-touch absorption capacity under fragile liquidity states. More broadly, the paper provides reduced-form evidence that short-horizon execution risk in highfrequency limit-order-book environments can be organized around economically interpretable local state variables rather than raw flow or static depth in isolation.

title: Artificial Effort
affiliations: University of Bergamo - University of Bergamo,, University of Bergamo, University of Bergamo - University of Bergamo, and University of Bergamo

detail.title: Artificial Effort

declarations.funderStatement: University of Bergamo Seedcorn Grant 2025

detail.abstract: Real-effort tasks, in which participants perform cognitively costly activities whose outcomes depend on actual performance, are widely used in experimental economics. Their validity, however, rests on the assumption that a human performs them. We study whether this assumption still holds in the era of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs). Using 8 canonical real-effort tasks and 23 LLMs from three major providers, we show that most tasks can now be solved accurately and at a negligible cost, while only a few resist automation. Performance improves with each model generation, and midtier models are rapidly closing the gap with frontier ones, broadening the set of widely accessible models that can automate these tasks. Additionally, we show that verbally offering monetary incentives has no effect on LLM performance. Our findings establish a boundary condition for the use of real-effort tasks in unsupervised settings: when participants can cheaply outsource task completion to an LLM, observed performance may no longer reflect genuine human effort.

detail.abstract: Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) are integral to economic development in global economies,  contributing significantly to infrastructure, employment, and strategic industries. However,  their financial health is often compromised by inefficiencies, regulatory constraints, and external economic pressures. PSUs are characteristically over-leveraged, asset-heavy, and structurally reliant on government grants instead of internally generated cash flows, rendering the standard private sector financial analysis frameworks ill-suited for their evaluation. The absence of a structured, integrated methodology for assessing PSU financial health represents a critical gap in the literature. This paper proposes a unique tripartite framework that combines financial ratio analysis, multiple and simple linear regression models, and the Altman Z"-Score  (2006 version, adapted for non-manufacturing firms). The framework offers a comprehensive assessment of efficiency, liquidity, and profitability, and links these dimensions to distress risk through grouped regression analysis, tailored specifically for non-manufacturing, privately administered public sector units. Through an extensive literature review, this paper establishes the fragmentation in existing approaches and demonstrates the framework's novelty and institutional relevance. The methodology is presented in full, including all formulae, ratio definitions, regression structures, and robustness diagnostics. For policymakers, the framework enables more granular and evidence-based decision-making on institutional reform, capital allocation, and long-term sustainability. Future research could extend this framework to incorporate advanced machine learning techniques for distress prediction or develop sector-  specific ratio benchmarks for common categories of PSUs.

detail.abstract:
The study investigates the psychological and social determinants of saving behavior among

university students. The PLS-SEM examines how financial literacy, parental influence, peer impact, and

self-control affect students' saving behavior. The observed significant variance suggests that the model

effectively accounts for students' saving behavior. The study reveals that financial literacy had the

greatest impact on savings behavior, demonstrating the importance of financial knowledge and

awareness. Parental Influence positively and significantly affects saving behavior, suggesting the

relevance of family socialization and practice modeling in teaching the children to save. Because Peer

Influence is insignificant, the saving decision is likely family-driven rather than societal. Unexpectedly,

self-control negatively affects saving behavior, challenging the conventional assumption and interplay

of discipline and action. These findings support Katona’s Theory and Life-Cycle Hypothesis that

psychological and social factors affect student’s early financial expectations and goals. Current study

adds to youth financial behavior literature, offering evidence-based advice on raising financially

responsible children.

title:
From Outputs to Trajectories: Systemic Behavioral Pathologies in Large Language Models
Rethinking Evaluation beyond the Output-based Paradigm

detail.title:
From Outputs to Trajectories: Systemic Behavioral Pathologies in Large Language Models
Rethinking Evaluation beyond the Output-based Paradigm
detail.abstract:
This paper builds on a prior conceptual analysis by the author, extending its analytical framework
through a trajectory-based perspective on large language model (LLM) behavior.
This paper argues that the behavior of large language models (LLMs) cannot be adequately
understood through output-based evaluation frameworks, which assess individual responses in
isolation. While such approaches are effective in measuring local performance, they fail to capture
the temporal and interactional dynamics through which system behavior unfolds across extended
exchanges.
Drawing on approximately 250 hours of longitudinal interaction with a state-of-the-art LLM, this
study develops a trajectory-based perspective, in which system behavior is conceptualized as an
emergent process distributed across sequences of responses rather than reducible to discrete outputs.
Within this framework, the paper identifies four systemic behavioral pathologies that remain largely
invisible under standard evaluation protocols: Dual Standards, Constitutional AI Theater, Möbius
Vulnerability, and Memory Asymmetry.
These phenomena are not characterized by isolated errors, but by process-dependent distortions that
emerge and stabilize across interaction trajectories. Each step in the interaction may appear locally
coherent, aligned, and plausible, while the trajectory as a whole becomes epistemically unstable,
normatively inconsistent, or structurally misaligned. This introduces a critical distinction between
local alignment and global misalignment, revealing a fundamental limitation in current approaches to
AI evaluation.
The paper shows that existing evaluation practices, which rely on short, decontextualized exchanges,
are structurally incapable of detecting these trajectory-level failures. As a result, system reliability
may be systematically overestimated, while underlying behavioral instabilities remain unobserved.
The analysis suggests that what is often interpreted as improved performance may, in fact, contribute
to the invisibility of deeper structural issues.
Building on these findings, the paper argues for a shift from output-centric to trajectory-aware
evaluation frameworks. Such frameworks would require extended interaction testing, temporal
consistency checks, and the reconstruction of interaction histories as coherent analytical objects.
More broadly, the paper contributes to ongoing debates on AI alignment, governance, and epistemic
reliability by introducing temporality as a central dimension in the analysis of AI systems.
By reframing LLM behavior as a time-dependent process rather than a sequence of independent
outputs, this work proposes a new analytical lens for understanding the limits of current AI systems
and the conditions necessary for more robust and reliable forms of alignment.

title: Trade-Induced Resource Substitution and Domestic Reallocation: Evidence from China's Wood Imports after WTO Accession

detail.title: Trade-Induced Resource Substitution and Domestic Reallocation: Evidence from China's Wood Imports after WTO Accession
detail.abstract: Using China's post-World Trade Organization surge in wood imports, this study examines the impact of resource imports on domestic economies when imported goods enter upstream segments of a local value chain. A resource-import shock activates three local margins: extraction contracts, processing expands, and labor reallocates with downstream technology. Using a shift-share design that combines pre-2001 import shares with subsequent product-level import growth, a one-percent rise in city-level wood imports raises forest coverage by 0.035% and worsens local air quality, while urban employment falls despite rising industrial output, a pattern of signs consistent with capital-biased downstream adjustments.

detail.abstract: Every time a medicine changes hands between manufacturer and patient in India, someone takes a cut. By the time that journey ends at a retail counter, the price has often grown three to five times beyond what the factory charged. This paper proposes a Government-Regulated Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) Pharmaceutical Distribution and Pricing Portal-a web and mobile-based system through which citizens can order medicines from a government-managed inventory at regulated prices, bypassing the layered intermediary network that drives costs up. The portal draws on the economic logic of India's Jan Aushadhi scheme but adds a digital layer: real-time price transparency, blockchain-verified drug authentication, and a central data backbone called IPDMS 2.0. A pricing simulation built around a representative chronic disease patient's monthly medicine basket suggests savings of approximately 56 percent compared to retail pharmacy prices-around ₹30,240 annually per household. The study evaluates the portal's technical architecture, supply chain efficiency gains, and last-mile delivery challenges, concluding that the proposed model is both economically viable and technically feasible within India's existing digital infrastructure.

title: Environmental performance and renewable resources: The impact on economic growth in the emerging and developing economies
affiliations: University of Perugia

detail.title: Environmental performance and renewable resources: The impact on economic growth in the emerging and developing economies
detail.abstract: This study aligns with the investigation of the impacts of environmental performance and renewable resources on economic growth in emerging and developing economies by using panel data covering the period 2000-2020 and by employing the clustering provided by the World Bank Group based on country income level (low, lower-middle, and upper-middle). Control variables included foreign direct investment inflows, trade openness, urbanization, and, in an original way, the country policy and institutional assessment (CPIA) index as a proxy for the quality of institutional and business environment, which effectively measures the extent to which a country’s governance supports sustainable development. The analysis has employed fixed-effects models (FE) and second-generation panel estimators for robustness checks, such as the Mean Group (MG) and Pooled Mean Group (PMG). The Dumitrescu-Hurlin panel causality test was also implemented. The results indicate that higher carbon intensity correlates with lower per-capita income, implying that carbon-intensive production systems hinder growth. Additionally, renewables use shows a statistically significant negative effect on growth, reflecting adjustment costs in countries with limited institutional capacity like emerging and developing economies. Overall, the findings have confirmed the existence of a trade-off between economic growth and environmental performance in emerging and developing economies.

title: Graduate Unemployment and the Wrong Remedy: Evaluating Indonesia's Study Program Closure Policy
affiliations: Bandung Institute of Technology - School of Business and Management

detail.title: Graduate Unemployment and the Wrong Remedy: Evaluating Indonesia's Study Program Closure Policy
detail.abstract: When a state decides which universities survive based on what employers will pay for, it has already answered the most fundamental question in educational philosophy without asking it. This theoretical policy analysis examines Indonesia’s study program closure policy, under which programs whose graduates fail employment absorption thresholds may be reviewed and closed. However, the assumption driving this decision remains unexamined on its most critical ground: whether employment absorption is a legitimate evaluative standard at all. The April 2026 policy announcement makes this question urgent because closure is no longer a theoretical possibility but an administrative instrument. This paper applies critical policy analysis using qualitative document analysis and comparative philosophical hermeneutics to evaluate the closure policy against Ki Hadjar Dewantara’s formative education philosophy, Raden Mas Panji Sosrokartono’s inner formation tradition, and democratic liberal education theory. The analysis finds that the policy fails all three frameworks simultaneously. It abandons students the Indonesian state has a historical obligation to protect, contradicts the philosophical tradition carried by the ministry’s own institutional inheritance, and applies an educational remedy to an industrial policy failure the state has not resolved. Thus, this paper shows that indigenous Indonesian educational philosophy constitutes a rigorous normative instrument for contemporary policy analysis. Moreover, it argues that closing study programs on employment grounds does not reform education; it shifts responsibility for a state-level economic failure onto educational institutions.

title: Structural Role Discovery in Networks with Tri-Channel GNNs
affiliations: Izmir University of Economics and Izmir University of Economics

detail.title: Structural Role Discovery in Networks with Tri-Channel GNNs
detail.abstract: Structural role discovery aims to identify nodes occupying similar functional positions in a network, independent of spatial proximity or community membership. Existing methods often struggle to jointly capture directional structural patterns and global role characteristics in complex networks. To address this limitation, we propose a fully unsupervised framework, tri-channel integrated graph embedding for roles (TIGER). TIGER explicitly models incoming, outgoing, and bidirectional interactions to learn direction-aware role representations. It aligns local message passing with global role similarity through a unified objective, while separating local structural inputs from global role descriptors to reduce information leakage and encourage genuine role inference. We also introduce RSS-Δ (Role Similarity Score), a metric for evaluating global role separability in embedding space, and use it together with proxy-kNN and silhouette scores to assess complementary aspects of embedding quality. Experiments on synthetic and real-world networks, including directed role-based stochastic block models, path-oriented graphs, karate, and transportation networks, show that TIGERachieves strong and interpretable role representations. Additional scalability and component-wise analyses further confirm the contribution of the tri-channel design. Compared with existing methods, TIGER better balances local coherence, global separability, and directional structural information, demonstrating its effectiveness for unsupervised role discovery in directed and undirected networks.

title: Walking the Tightrope: Post Merger Performance Pressure,Organizational Complexity, and their Role in CEO Financial Reporting Fraud
affiliations: University of South Florida - School of Accountancy, University of South Florida and Andrews University

detail.title: Walking the Tightrope: Post Merger Performance Pressure,Organizational Complexity, and their Role in CEO Financial Reporting Fraud
detail.abstract: Drawing from Schnatterly et al.’s (2018) framework, we demonstrate how organizational complexity and performance pressure create opportunities for Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) to engage in financial reporting fraud within the context of mergers and acquisitions (M&As).  Using the Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) Accounting and Auditing Enforcement Releases (1991-2016) we find firms engaging in M&As are more likely to commit financial reporting fraud (FRF). More importantly, this propensity is exacerbated by the organizational complexity associated with diversified deals, larger acquisitions, and multiple M&As, as well as the pressure from institutional investors and product market competition (PMC). We also find that the monitoring role of analysts outweighs their external pressure on CEOs, reducing the likelihood of reporting fraud. Our findings suggest that the intricate dynamics of M&As, along with heightened performance pressures are major factors that prompt CEOs to resort to FRF.

title: A Contract Theory–Driven Adaptive Incentive Mechanism for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
affiliations: Hebei University
