title: Finding the Optimal Sensor Layout for Structure Health Monitoring using Simultaneous Bayesian Updating with Structural Reliability Methods
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Wuhan University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Finding the Optimal Sensor Layout for Structure Health Monitoring using Simultaneous Bayesian Updating with Structural Reliability Methods
detail.abstract: Optimal sensor placement on engineering structures (e.g., dams, bridges) is critical for accurate structural performance characterization. However, combinatorial explosion occurs when selecting candidate sensor layouts—even for a small number of sensors—rendering brute force (exhaustive) optimization computationally prohibitive. This study addresses this problem by introducing a novel Bayesian updating framework, called Simultaneous Bayesian Updating with Structural Reliability Methods (SBUS). SBUS efficiently derives posterior distributions for all possible sensor layouts in a single computational run, eliminating iterative executions. Information entropies for all possible layouts are quantified, and the sensor layout with the minimum information entropy, or the least uncertainties, is chosen as the optimal sensor layout. This approach guarantees theoretical optimality as all possible sensor layouts are exhaustively explored. The proposed method is demonstrated and validated using earth dam and cantilever beam case studies, demonstrating the method's effectiveness in finding the optimal sensor layout. The results indicate that, although adding sensors could reduce uncertainties in parameter estimation, its marginal utility becomes negligible as the number of sensors increases, implying that it may be unnecessary to install too many sensors on an engineering structure. Instead, optimal layout of a limited number of sensors can achieve comparable performance of many sensors.

title: Separating uncertainty sources using a hierarchical Bayesian approach with scientific machine learning of implicit yield surface models
affiliations: University of Utah, Sandia National Laboratories, Sandia National Laboratories, Sandia National Laboratories, Sandia National Laboratories and Sandia National Laboratories

detail.title: Separating uncertainty sources using a hierarchical Bayesian approach with scientific machine learning of implicit yield surface models
detail.abstract: Observed material behavior is stochastic in nature due to intrinsic material variability and extrinsic sensor noise, for example, both of which contribute to aleatoric uncertainty. In practice, selecting an existing material constitutive model defines a model form, introducing epistemic uncertainty. Once that model form is selected, calibration of its parameters lumps all aleatoric sources together, precluding the ability to model specifically the intrinsic material variability. This work aims to implement a method for separating these sources of aleatoric uncertainty, specifically for implicit yield surface models, whilst minimizing epistemic uncertainty caused by the model form. We achieve this using a genetic programming-based symbolic regression (GPSR) approach that uses a multi-objective fitness function, MOSR, and training data generated from synthetic microstructure simulation. This function considers both an implicit fitness metric (ISR) and a statistical metric, the marginal likelihood, to select models that fit the data while also avoiding overfitting to noise in the dataset. We also employ a multi-tree parent acyclic graph (MPA) approach to regularize the GPSR algorithm and ensure that models adhere to the known physics of the material. Once a model is found, we employ a hierarchical Bayesian approach, learning the extrinsic sensor noise distributions via sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) estimates conducted on a single microstructure at a time, thereby eliminating any intrinsic material variability. We can then conduct SMC on the complete set of microstructures to learn the intrinsic variability. We test our method on a verification problem, first learning the exact Gurson-Tvergaard-Needleman (GTN) model with known aleatoric uncertainties. Then, we apply the method to learn a new yield surface model for a more complex material microstructure, reducing the epistemic uncertainty through a more optimal model form and characterizing the distinct aleatoric uncertainties present in the simulation data. The results demonstrate that our method can identify new, physically valid yield surface models and accurately quantify the distinct aleatoric uncertainties contained in the data. This method will allow us to learn new yield surface models even when data are noisy, and improve the interpretability and understanding of the mechanics and variability of the material being modeled.

title: A Hybrid Bayesian-Markov Model for Time-Dependent Risk Assessment of Hydrocarbon Storage Tank Farms
affiliations: China University of Petroleum (East China), China University of Petroleum (East China), Hohai University, China University of Petroleum (East China) and China University of Petroleum (East China)

detail.title: A Hybrid Bayesian-Markov Model for Time-Dependent Risk Assessment of Hydrocarbon Storage Tank Farms
detail.abstract: With the accelerated expansion of the chemical industry, liquid hydrocarbons have emerged as critical organic chemical feedstocks with substantial market demand. However, these substances are characterized by inherent flammability and explosivity. Consequently, liquid hydrocarbon spherical tank farms are frequently classified as major hazard installations within petrochemical complexes, presenting significant risks of fire, explosion, and subsequent domino-effect propagation. This underscores the necessity for rigorous research into the process risks associated with these facilities. In this study, a Bayesian Network (BN) model was developed to evaluate initial accident risks. By integrating evidence theory, real-time process data were utilized to facilitate the dynamic identification of critical risk factors under specific operational scenarios. Furthermore, statistical failure data were refined through accident precursor theory, allowing for an objective reflection of system characteristics and a dynamic assessment of safety levels and consequence probabilities. To account for temporal variations, node time-dependency was incorporated, and a reliability degradation model for critical equipment was constructed using Markov chain theory. This approach simulated state transition processes over time to derive precise transition probabilities. Utilizing a Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN) framework, the study achieved a temporal assessment of tank farm process risks. Finally, fuzzy consequence loss rates were employed to quantify severity, which, when integrated with calculated probabilities, provided a comprehensive and dynamic risk assessment.

title: Reliability models and exceedance statistics based on convex combinations of order statistics
affiliations: Wageningen University & Research

detail.title: Reliability models and exceedance statistics based on convex combinations of order statistics
detail.abstract: We consider a new model of a coherent system whose lifetime is a convex combination of two consecutive order statistics. We study the distribution and reliability function of this system with new structure-function. It is shown that the inspection time of the n-k+1-out-of-n system between failure times of two components can also be described by this convex combination. The distribution of time between the inspection and failure times is studied. The distributions of exceedance statistics based on the convex combinations of consecutive order statistics are also presented. The applications of results in reliability engineering, economics, and environmental sciences are discussed. Some illustrative examples and graphs are presented.

title: External Debt, broad money growth and macroeconomic performance in the GCC economies: A panel regression approach
affiliations: University of Bahrain

detail.title: External Debt, broad money growth and macroeconomic performance in the GCC economies: A panel regression approach
detail.abstract: This study aims to provide robust empirical evidence on the relationship between broad money growth, external debt, inflation, trade openness and economic growth using panel data. This study uses a balanced panel of GCC countries from 2010 to 2025 and harmonized data from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) database. A multi-step econometric framework is applied using unbalanced panel data. The panel unit root test, followed by fixed-effect estimations and robustness checks employing heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, cross-sectional dependence, and the dynamic panel Generalized Method of Moments (GMM), are employed to control dynamic persistence in economic growth. Under the fixed-effects estimation, broad money growth has a positive and statistically significant relationship with economic growth, implying that higher monetary expansion leads to better growth performance within countries over time. External debt shows a negative and highly significant coefficient, suggesting that increasing debt leads to slower economic growth. The dynamic panel GMM results confirm the robustness of these findings. The study findings highlight the importance of managing external debt and stable macroeconomic conditions for sustainable economic growth, suggesting that more open economies may engage more actively in external financing. Modest monetary expansion boosts economic activity by reducing liquidity constraints, encouraging investment, and promoting credit expansion. The added value of this paper lies in the contributions to improving our knowledge of how external sector dynamics influence economic performance in a region characterized by chronic external shocks and structural upheaval.

title: US Stock Market Network Analysis for Crisis Prediction
affiliations: Paris Dauphine University, Students

detail.title: US Stock Market Network Analysis for Crisis Prediction
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether the topology of stock correlation networks conveys predictive information about future equity market crises. We model the cross-sectional dependence structure of large-cap U.S. equities as a dynamic weighted graph, constructed from rolling Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage correlation matrices with exponential time-weighting, and threshold these matrices to retain economically meaningful co-movement links. We extract two complementary feature sets: graph-level network statistics summarising the global topology at each date, and time-series features capturing the dynamics of the market return distribution over multiple horizons. These features serve as inputs to a binary classification framework that predicts whether the forward 21-day maximum drawdown will exceed a crisis threshold, evaluated strictly out-of-sample through an expanding walk-forward crossvalidation scheme. In addition to the predictive exercise, we construct a panel of per-stock network centrality measures: degree, strength, clustering, eigenvector centrality, PageRank, and community membership that can serve as the basis for cross-sectional investment strategies. Our methodology provides a replicable, modular pipeline for translating network topology into actionable financial signals.

title: Home-Market Advantage and the EV Transition in European Car Markets, 2010-2024
affiliations: Carl von Ossietzky University of Oldenburg

detail.title: Home-Market Advantage and the EV Transition in European Car Markets, 2010-2024
detail.abstract: Passenger cars account for roughly 15\% of EU CO\textsubscript{2} emissions, and member-state purchase subsidies for battery-electric vehicles (EVs) are among the largest demand-side climate-policy instruments now deployed in Europe. A central question for European energy and climate policy is whether these technology-neutral subsidies translate uniformly into cleaner fleets, or whether a persistent home-market bias in car sales shapes which brands absorb the subsidy-induced EV growth, with consequences for the geographic incidence of emission reductions, industrial rents, and the political durability of the transition. Using brand-level new-car registrations for all EU-27 countries over 2010--2024 and a continuous country-year measure of direct EV purchase subsidies, I estimate gravity-style Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood (PPML) regressions and a dynamic difference-in-differences design for continuous, non-absorbing treatment. Domestic brands enjoy a large sales premium overall, a markedly smaller premium in the EV segment, and lose relative EV market share as subsidies rise: each additional euro of purchase subsidy is associated with higher domestic EV volumes on the extensive margin but a declining domestic share of the EV market on the intensive margin, with foreign EV specialists capturing a disproportionate part of the subsidy-induced growth. Demand-side EV subsidies can therefore deliver emission reductions while leaving a non-trivial share of industrial gains abroad, suggesting complementary supply-side policies where governments pursue both decarbonization and domestic production.

title: Income Distribution and Extensive Margin of Trade: The Effect of Inequality on Product Variety
affiliations: Osaka Sangyo University - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Income Distribution and Extensive Margin of Trade: The Effect of Inequality on Product Variety

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was not supported by any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between income inequality and the number of imported varieties under the assumption of hierarchic demand. Using a panel dataset of 135 countries over the period 2012-2024, I estimate the effect of the Gini index of the importing country on the extensive margin of trade. The theoretical model demonstrates that an increase in income inequality reduces the number of imported varieties in the aggregate. The empirical results show that the negative effect of income inequality on imported varieties varies with the income level of the importing country and is statistically significant only for high-income countries. This finding is robust to instrumental variable estimation using the newspaper titles share lagged by 10 years, which accounts for the potential endogeneity of the Gini index. Furthermore, among income groups, only an increase in the bottom 50% income share is shown to significantly raise imported varieties in high-income countries, carrying important implications for redistribution policy. These findings suggest that rising income inequality prevents the extensive margin from expanding and may reduce overall economic welfare.

title: The Green Shield: The Intersectional Role of Agriculture in Combatting Sexual Violence in Northern Ghana
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Green Shield: The Intersectional Role of Agriculture in Combatting Sexual Violence in Northern Ghana
detail.abstract:
Abstract

Northern Ghana is simultaneously one of the most agriculturally productive and conflict-affected regions in West Africa. Chieftaincy succession disputes — most notably the decades-long Dagbon crisis that culminated in the assassination of the Ya Na (King of Dagbon) in 2002 — farmer-herder conflicts that have intensified as desertification advances, and pervasive gender-based violence together constitute an interlocking conflict ecology that suppresses agricultural output, displaces communities, and disproportionately harms women and girls. In Gushegu District alone, police and chieftaincy records document 16 farmer-herder conflict cases, 17 armed robberies, and 22 rape cases involving herders between 2010 and 2022. The Dagbon chieftaincy conflict is estimated to have caused a 30 percent decline in agricultural output and a 50 percent drop in trade in affected areas. Domestic violence alone costs countries 1.2 to 2 percent of GDP — the equivalent of most nations' spending on primary education.

This paper examines whether and how structured participation in agricultural value chains — specifically in shea, moringa, fonio, tiger nuts, and other indigenous crops — can serve as a pathway out of both poverty and conflict for women and youth in Northern Ghana. Drawing on a systematic literature review of value chain interventions across sub-Saharan Africa, conflict analysis literature specific to Northern Ghana, and the programme evidence base of the Social Innovation Africa (SIA) C.J. Walker Feminist Industrialisation Hubs model, the paper argues that agro-processing hubs represent a distinctive form of economic peacebuilding: creating safe   physical spaces for women's enterprise, generating income that reduces women's vulnerability to violence, and building cross-community economic interdependencies that reduce the incentive structures driving conflict.

The paper develops an original analytical framework — the Conflict-Value Chain-Empowerment (CVCE) nexus — to theorise how women's structured economic participation in high-value indigenous food systems disrupts the poverty-conflict-vulnerability cycle. It concludes with five policy recommendations aligned with Ghana's post-conflict reconstruction frameworks, the ECOWAS supplementary act on smallholder farmers, and the UN Security Council Resolution 1325 on Women, Peace and Security.

title: Grant Management Capacity in African Institutions: Systems, Determinants and Operational Challenges
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Grant Management Capacity in African Institutions: Systems, Determinants and Operational Challenges
detail.abstract: BackgroundGrant management is important for transparency and accountability in preventing fraud, waste, misuse of funds, and research funding. Inadequate grant management capacity is a major problem that African institutions have continuously faced for decades. They continue to experience substantial gaps in grants management which include human resources, governance, and financial management. Methods The study adopted a cross-sectional design and was conducted in 20 African countries. The quantitative aspect of the study targeted institutional grant managers who had more than three years experience in grant management. Purposive sampling was used to obtain a sample size of 212 institutions. The data were analysed using STATA version 18.0. The qualitative aspect targeted institutional heads and directors of research. For qualitative aspect, purposive sampling was also used to select the study participants. The data were analysed thematically in NVIVO software. Results The Good Financial Grant Practices (GFGP) was the most common adopted standard among African institutions, 49.5% (n=105). Institutions which had adopted an international standard e.g. GFGP in grant management were 3.84 times more likely to have capacity in grants management, [AOR=3.84; CI:1.26,11.71; p-value: 0.02]. Additionally, institutions which had effective grant management systems were 13.29 times more likely to have capacity in grants management [AOR=13.29; CI:2.79,63.18; p-value: < 0.01]. ConclusionThis study demonstrates that strengthening the capacity in grant management among African institutions requires more than siloed improvements in trainings and staffing; it demands a comprehensive, multifaceted approach anchored in international standards, efficient and fully automated grant management systems, and adequate staffing.

title: An Empirical Analysis of the Efficiency of China's A-Share Market: Weak-Form and Semi-Strong-Form Evidence from the CSI 300 Index

detail.title: An Empirical Analysis of the Efficiency of China's A-Share Market: Weak-Form and Semi-Strong-Form Evidence from the CSI 300 Index
detail.abstract: This paper examines the informational efficiency of China's A-share market using the CSI 300 Index over the period 11 April 2005 to 11 March 2020. Building on the Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH) and the Random Walk Hypothesis (RWH), the paper evaluates weak-form efficiency using four complementary tests: the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) unit-root test, the serial correlation test of error terms, the stock-price autocorrelation test, and the Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio test. Semi-strong-form efficiency is assessed through an event-study framework focused on the market response to real interest-rate changes. The results indicate that the A-share market has generally reached a weak-form efficient level in the short run, but that this conclusion weakens over longer horizons. The variance ratio results show increasing rejection of the random-walk null as the lag length increases, suggesting medium-and long-term predictability. The semi-strong-form test indicates that unexpected changes in interest rates are not absorbed by stock returns immediately; instead, the response is gradual and partially excessive. The evidence therefore supports the conclusion that China's A-share market is weak-form efficient only conditionally and has not yet attained semi-strong-form efficiency. These findings are consistent with the structural characteristics of China's market, including high retail participation, information asymmetry, evolving disclosure quality, and continuing institutional reform.

title: Do earnings call transcripts predict post-announcement returns?
affiliations: Paris Dauphine University, Students

detail.title: Do earnings call transcripts predict post-announcement returns?
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether earnings call transcripts contain information that is predictive of post-announcement idiosyncratic stock returns. We construct a systematic machine learning pipeline that transforms raw transcript text into quantitative signals and evaluates their out-of-sample forecasting performance on the Russell 1000 universe. We extract two families of text representations, sparse TF-IDF bag-of-words features on preprocessed transcripts, and dense semantic embeddings from the pre-trained sentence transformer all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and combine them with traditional finance-specific sentiment scores derived from the Loughran-McDonald dictionary. For each earnings event, targets are defined as multi-horizon cumulative idiosyncratic returns (residuals from a rolling CAPM estimated exclusively on pre-filing data) at horizons of 1, 3, 5 and 21 trading days. Model training and evaluation follow a strict quarterly walk-forward cross validation scheme that eliminates forward-looking bias by design. We compare three feature compositions across four regression models (Ridge, Lasso, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) and evaluate performance using directional accuracy, long-short spread, and an interpretable excess-RMSE relative to the CAPM null model. This framework allows us to systematically identify which combination of text representation, prediction horizon, and model architecture extracts the most economically meaningful signals from earnings calls.

title: Foreign Eyes on Wall Street: Investor Attention and U.S. Stock Reactions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Lehigh University - Business School and University of Birmingham

detail.title: Foreign Eyes on Wall Street: Investor Attention and U.S. Stock Reactions
detail.abstract: We show that foreign investor attention is a key driver of U.S. stock market movements. Using SEC EDGAR search activity matched to investor location, we provide the first firm-level evidence that foreign, rather than domestic, information acquisition predicts abnormal returns. A 10% increase in foreign EDGAR searches is associated with a 0.9 percentage point increase in abnormal daily returns for S&P 500 firms. The effect is strongest for firms with opaque information environments and greater exposure to China. Focusing on China—the dominant source of foreign attention—we exploit lunar calendar holidays as an instrument that generates exogenous variation in attention. The results support a causal interpretation and reveal economically large return predictability. We further show that foreign financial policies, including China’s Stock Connect program, shape investor attention and transmit shocks to U.S. asset prices.

title: A Governance Assessment Framework for Nascent Space Sectors: Adapting the Space Development Ladder for Developing Economies

detail.title: A Governance Assessment Framework for Nascent Space Sectors: Adapting the Space Development Ladder for Developing Economies
detail.abstract: Frameworks for assessing national space development have focused on technological milestones such as satellite capabilities and launch capacity. While useful for tracking hardware progression, these instruments do not capture the governance conditions that shape whether developing countries can sustain their space activities. This article proposes an adapted framework that integrates governance milestones into the Space Technology Ladder developed by Wood and Weigel. The instrument identifies nineteen milestones across five development levels (Nascent, Low, Regular, Medium, and High), incorporating items such as national space policy adoption, the institutional nature of the space agency, regional organization membership, public-private partnerships, and governance architecture. Applied to Peru as an illustrative case, the framework reveals that nine of nineteen milestones have been achieved, with gaps concentrated in governance and institutional categories rather than technological ones. Peru has acquired satellite capabilities, deployed university nanosatellites, and maintained cooperation agreements with NASA and APSCO without a national space policy or governance framework. The adapted framework makes this asymmetry between technical capacity and institutional architecture visible, producing findings that a technology-only assessment would miss. The instrument is offered as a replicable tool for researchers and policymakers working on space development in emerging economies.

title: Shadow Lobbying During Tax Audits
affiliations: University of Florida - Fisher School of Accounting

detail.title: Shadow Lobbying During Tax Audits
detail.abstract: Data from the Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995 (LDA) suggest corporate lobbying is modest, identifying fewer than 10% of public corporations as having lobbied the government in the past thirty years. Anecdotes from watchdogs instead suggest significant corporate lobbying occurs without disclosure because of limitations in the LDA (commonly referred to as shadow lobbying). Shadow lobbying is poorly understood because it is difficult to observe. In this paper, I examine corporate lobbying in the setting of tax audits and quantify the extent to which such activity is disclosed through the LDA. To obtain a non-disclosure mediated measure of suspected lobbying activity, I spatially intersect 4.5 trillion pings from the movement of 179 million smartphones to building shapes and examine in-person interactions among firms, lobbyists, and IRS officials in 2019. I exploit the launch of three issue-based IRS audit campaigns and show that affected firms significantly increased in-person visits to the national headquarters of the IRS through contract lobbyists, trade associations, and in-house lobbyists. Approximately 40% of firms that initiated such contacts disclosed no lobbying, with nondisclosure prevalent among both in-house and trade-association lobbyists. These results suggest limits in existing disclosure policy allows substantial corporate political interaction to occur in private.

detail.abstract:
This paper operationalizes a general framework of value creation as a sequence of non-expansive transformations of usable energy by introducing measurable indicators of structural efficiency. We define transformation efficiency, structural loss, and bottleneck conditions in a matrix-based dynamic system.

A stylized supply chain model demonstrates that reductions in downstream transformation efficiency lead to delayed and limited value accumulation. Comparative simulations show that the gap between baseline and shock scenarios increases over time, indicating cumulative structural inefficiency. In parallel, the total usable energy norm declines more rapidly under shock, reflecting accelerated dissipation.

These results show that value creation can be quantitatively analyzed as a function of transformation structure rather than resource quantity alone.

detail.abstract: This paper presents the Temporal Warfare framework an independent geostrategic theoretical system developed over four years (2022-2026), examining the structural transformation of modern conflict within the Global Flow System. The framework advances five interconnected propositions across five parts. Part I establishes that the foundational unit of the modern world is not space but flow: energy, logistics, information, and capital operating as interconnected flow fields. Part II demonstrates that these flows are not merely conditions of operation but weapons. Part III introduces the vortex a self-reinforcing disturbance state-and identifies three vortex types currently active: distortion (Ukraine), exhaustion (Persian Gulf), and severance (East Asia). Part IV maps the financial layer as the system's measuring instrument, where all disruptions converge and are translated into the price of time. Part V Heliostrategy steps outside the terrestrial framework entirely, arguing that the acquisition of the Solar System has begun, that the decisive measure of great power status is shifting from nuclear deterrence to space capability (defined as the simultaneous possession of transportation, energy, and compute capacity beyond Earth), and that the base of power is undergoing its sixth historical transformation: from physical force through agricultural knowledge, land, capital, and data to space presence. The framework introduces several original concepts, including the Global Flow System, flow-based warfare, vortex dynamics and the vortex spectrum (micro, meso, macro), the financial layer as the price of time, the learning asymmetry between actors who understand the flow system and those who do not, the space-capable great power, and the Lagrange point as a literal (not metaphorical) strategic concept. The paper argues that classical geostrategy asks who controls space, Temporal Warfare asks who controls time, and Heliostrategy asks who can step outside the system and found a new one.

title: The Impact of Capital Market Liberalization on the Rational Valuation of A-Shares: Evidence from the Shanghai-Hong Kong and Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect Programs

detail.title: The Impact of Capital Market Liberalization on the Rational Valuation of A-Shares: Evidence from the Shanghai-Hong Kong and Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect Programs
detail.abstract: This study examines whether capital market liberalization improves the rational valuation of China's A-share market. It focuses on the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect and Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect as quasi-natural opening events that progressively reduced cross-border investment frictions while preserving a controlled institutional architecture. Using the Hsiao, Ching, and Wan (2012) panel-data counterfactual model, the paper estimates the price-to-earnings ratio that the CSI 800 Index would have displayed in the absence of each policy and compares simulated values with observed outcomes. The findings show that the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect did not immediately reduce A-share valuation levels; rather, the actual CSI 800 price-toearnings ratio remained above its counterfactual path during the short and medium term, partly because the 2014-2015 boom and subsequent correction dominated the policy effect. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect also failed to generate a sharp immediate correction, but its longer-run trajectory is more consistent with gradual valuation rationalization. The results indicate that liberalization mechanisms improve valuation rationality only when foreign participation, disclosure discipline, investor learning, and market microstructure reforms accumulate over time. The study contributes to the literature on emerging-market liberalization by linking Stock Connect reforms to aggregate valuation rationality rather than only liquidity, volatility, segmentation, or price informativeness. It also offers policy implications for future liberalization initiatives, including broader Connect programs, investor protection, accounting transparency, and the development of value-oriented domestic institutional investors.

title: Directional Dynamics, Fragility Geometry, and Cascade Inevitability in Multi-Environment Systems: A WLRT Framework
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Directional Dynamics, Fragility Geometry, and Cascade Inevitability in Multi-Environment Systems: A WLRT Framework
detail.abstract:
This paper develops a structural framework for system evolution in multi-environment settings within the Wave Liquidity Redistribution Theory (WLRT).

The framework introduces three core components: directional stability, fragility surface, and cascade inevitability. It shows that system dynamics are governed not by external forces or stochastic processes, but by internal structural constraints arising from configuration structure, Phase Time ordering, and inter-environment interactions.

Directional selection is determined by minimization of effective structural resistance. System trajectories follow locally optimal paths over a dynamic fragility surface. Phase transitions correspond to changes in admissible transitions and constraint density. Cascades occur when no stable local resolution remains available.

The results provide a unified structural interpretation of direction, stability, and abrupt transitions, and apply to any system admitting dual directed motion, including financial, informational, execution, and logistical environments.

detail.abstract: Agricultural decision-making is inherently shaped by risk and uncertainty arising from climatic variability, market volatility, financial instability and policy shifts. This chapter combines the conceptual foundations and analytical tools used to evaluate and manage such uncertainties within farm and policy contexts. It distinguishes between measurable risk and unmeasurable uncertainty, drawing on both classical economic theory and modern frameworks such as state-contingent and behavioural models. Quantitative illustrations such as Expected Monetary Value (EMV), Certainty Equivalent (CE) demonstrate how decision criteria translate uncertainty into measurable outcomes. The chapter also integrates contemporary developments, including digital risk management, AIbased forecasting and resilience-oriented policy design. Overall, it provides a comprehensive framework linking theoretical models, empirical evidence and practical strategies to strengthen agricultural decision-making under uncertainty.

detail.abstract:
This report presents a strategic analysis of Spain's structural position within the European energy transition, examining three interconnected dimensions that have received limited integrated treatment in existing literature.
First, it assesses Spain's renewable energy base — which reached 56.1% of mainland electricity generation in January 2026 — as a foundation for competitive green hydrogen production and export via the H2Med/BarMar corridor and the Bay of Biscay interconnector. Second, it introduces an original scenario-based financial simulation for a Gibraltar Green Maritime Fuel Hub, projecting annual steady-state revenues between EUR 1 billion and EUR 12 billion depending on IMO regulatory acceleration and infrastructure deployment pace — a dimension largely absent from current European energy policy literature. Third, it applies two original theoretical frameworks to Spain's domestic fiscal challenges: the Global Reflection Economic Theory (GRE) and the Double Trust Reflection Theory (DTRT), which reconceptualise public asset recycling and mutual citizen-state trust as measurable instruments for reducing sovereign debt costs and structural unemployment without austerity.
The analysis draws on verified primary data sources including Red Eléctrica de España, the European Investment Bank, the H2Med Project Consortium, and the International Maritime Organization. Findings suggest that Spain's three core strategic assets — renewable abundance, Gibraltar's geographic position, and complementary regional partnerships — generate maximum policy value only when treated as an integrated system rather than separate policy domains. The report concludes with seven sharp actionable recommendations and a phased strategic timeline for 2026.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces risk displacement as a distinct equilibrium outcome of fragmented regulatory authority, separable from coordination failure, regulatory arbitrage, and moral hazard. We develop a two-margin model in which risk-creating firms choose both total exposure and its allocation across jurisdictions that differ in enforcement credibility. Firms internalize compliance costs, expected sanctions, and private losses; regulators internalize enforcement costs and a share of social loss when risks materialize. The central result is a waterbed mechanism: tightening enforcement in one jurisdiction can raise system-wide risk by relocating exposure toward weakly enforced nodes. The relationship between regulatory intensity and systemic risk is non-monotonic but quantitatively asymmetric: the mitigation-dominant region is narrow and shallow, while the displacement-dominant region is wide and produces large increases in systemic exposure once enforcement variance crosses a threshold. We characterize the equilibrium under partial mobility, prove a corrected N-jurisdiction cascade with variance scaling (N-1) / N (bounded above by one), and embed regulator competition in the partial-mobility framework so that, under specified parameter restrictions, a smooth interior race-to-the-bottom equilibrium exists; we characterize the corner Nash that arises when the restriction fails. We complete the analysis with a welfare ranking across regimes (with explicit conditions for the ranking to hold) and five testable hypotheses tied to enforcement variance, mobility friction, observability, the number of regulatory jurisdictions, and cross-sectoral mobility heterogeneity. Policy implications follow from the welfare ranking and include enforcement harmonization, strategic mobility friction design, and cross-jurisdictional risk tracing.

title: A physics-constrained GA-BP neural network for contact fatigue life prediction of surface-strengthened transmission gears
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials, Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A physics-constrained GA-BP neural network for contact fatigue life prediction of surface-strengthened transmission gears
detail.abstract: Helicopter transmission gears operate under harsh high-speed, heavy-load, high-frequency alternating stress conditions, where contact fatigue failure accounts for most gear failures, critically limiting the reliability and service life of transmission systems. The shot peening (SP)-finishing composite process is a recognized high-efficiency synergistic surface strengthening technology for gear anti-fatigue manufacturing, yet the coupling mechanism between its multi-process parameters and surface integrity gradient characteristics has not been systematically clarified. Traditional fatigue life prediction methods fail to fully account for the gradient evolution of surface integrity induced by composite strengthening, causing significant prediction deviations for surface-treated gears. Meanwhile, pure data-driven intelligent models rely heavily on high-quality experimental data, are prone to local optima, and lack sufficient physical interpretability, severely restricting their engineering application in aviation gear life assessment. To address these gaps, this work develops an integrated framework combining multi-process experimental characterization, multi-scale coupled simulation integrating Johnson-Cook constitutive and ETMB dislocation density models, and a physics-constrained GA-BP neural network for contact fatigue life prediction of surface-treated 9310 steel gears. We quantitatively reveal the synergistic evolution of key surface integrity parameters under the SP-finishing process. The multi-scale model has high accuracy, with relative errors below 8% for residual stress and 10% for surface roughness. The proposed GA-BP model yields life prediction error within scatter band of 1.7, outperforming traditional BP networks. This study provides a framework for aviation gear process optimization, surface integrity regulation and high-precision life assessment, with important engineering value for anti-fatigue design of high-reliability gear components.

title: How the integration of Technology and Finance empowers urban-rural integration? A quasi-natural evidence from China

detail.title: How the integration of Technology and Finance empowers urban-rural integration? A quasi-natural evidence from China

keywords: Pilot Policy Promoting the Integration of Technology and Finance

detail.abstract: Technology and finance are critical drivers of high-quality economic development, yet their combined impact on the urban-rural integration remains underexplored. Using panel data for Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2000 to 2023, this study treats the “Pilot Policy Promoting the Integration of Technology and Finance” as a quasi-natural experiment and applies a staggered difference-in-differences method to estimate its impact on urban-rural integration. The results show that the pilot policy significantly enhance urban-rural integration, and this finding remains robust after a series of validity and robustness checks. Further analysis indicates that the pilot policy effectively improves the level of urban-rural integration through the mechanism of facilitating the flow of population and capital mobility, enhancing technological innovation, and promoting the rationalization of industrial structure. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the policy effects are more pronounced in eastern regions and in cities with stronger intellectual property protection. This study provides theoretical support and policy implications for further releasing the benefits of science and technology finance innovation and advancing urban-rural integration.

title: Day-Ahead Optimal Operation Strategy for Building-Integrated Energy Systems: An Engineering Application

detail.title: Day-Ahead Optimal Operation Strategy for Building-Integrated Energy Systems: An Engineering Application
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a day-ahead optimization strategy for building-type integrated energy systems (IES) in hot-summer and cold-winter regions. By employing a piecewise linearization method to address the nonlinear parameters of heating/cooling equipment, multi-energy flow collaborative optimization is achieved under typical summer and winter scenarios. Results show that during peak electricity price periods on typical summer days, the combined cooling, heating, and power (CCHP) unit operates at 100percent load rate, with thermal storage tanks ensuring peak cooling supply. The chiller unit operates near 50percent load during off-peak hours. In winter scenarios, thermal storage tanks and gas boilers prove more economical than CCHP during the off-peak electricity price period, while CCHP dominates during peak hours with gas boilers exceeding 80percent load rate, storing surplus thermal energy heat in thermal storage tanks. This strategy provides effective engineering guidance for optimizing electricity, gas, cooling, and heating multi-energy flows in building-type IES.

title: Optimal Investment and Entropy-Regularized Learning Under Stochastic Volatility Models with Portfolio Constraints
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Université Laval

detail.title: Optimal Investment and Entropy-Regularized Learning Under Stochastic Volatility Models with Portfolio Constraints
detail.abstract: We study the problem of optimal portfolio selection under stochastic volatility within a continuous-time reinforcement learning framework with portfolio constraints. Exploration is modeled through entropy-regularized relaxed controls, where the investor selects probability distributions over admissible portfolio allocations rather than deterministic strategies. Using dynamic programming arguments, we derive the associated entropy-regularized Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation, whose Hamiltonian involves optimization over probability measures supported on a compact control set. We show that the optimal exploratory policy takes the form of a truncated Gaussian distribution characterized by spatial derivatives of the solution of the resulting nonlinear quasilinear parabolic partial differential equation. Under suitable structural conditions on the model coefficients, we prove the existence of classical solutions to this nonlinear HJB equation for the value function.We then establish a verification theorem and analyze the policy-improvement structure induced by the entropy-regularized Hamiltonian, showing how the resulting sequence of PDEs provides a continuous-time interpretation of actor–critic learning dynamics. Finally, our PDE analysis with a semi-closed form of optimal value and optimal policy enables the design of an implementable reinforcement learning algorithm by recasting the optimal problem in a martingale framework.

title: Leverage Shocks, Market Frictions, and Downturn of China's Urban Housing Market
affiliations: , University of Washington - College of Built Environments, University of Hong Kong, University of Washington and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Leverage Shocks, Market Frictions, and Downturn of China's Urban Housing Market
detail.abstract: This study is among the first to investigate the role of deleveraging in the transition of China's urban housing market from a prolonged boom to a structural downturn between 2017 and 2024. Specifically, we investigate how supply-side exogenous deleveraging shocks contribute to the market downturn. Addressing significant data constraints regarding firm-level financial statements in China, we develop a Bartik type instrumental variable by matching the leverage, national sales and local sales of 111 listed real estate firms in 29 cities. The sample represents 38% of national GDP and 39% of the urban population, capturing the most credit-sensitive urban housing markets in China. Contrary to the co-movement of household leverage and housing price, our baseline result finds positive effects of deleveraging shocks for firms on housing price. Mechanism analysis reveals that this was driven by supply-side government and firm responses that neutralized downward pressure even as demandside fundamentals deteriorated. Specifically, increased land price by local governments, expanded pre-sale area by firms and local governments, and supply-reduction-driven passive destocking by firms decoupled price from market fundamentals during the real estate downturn in Chinese cities as of 2024. Comparative analysis indicates that price declines mainly occurred in markets with high valuations rather than weak economic fundamentals.

title: When Do Effective Tax Rates Measure Tax Avoidance? Evidence from Reporting-Induced Variation in Book Income
affiliations: University of Wollongong, University of Wollongong, School of Business and University of Wollongong - School of Accounting Economics and Finance

detail.title: When Do Effective Tax Rates Measure Tax Avoidance? Evidence from Reporting-Induced Variation in Book Income
detail.abstract: A large empirical literature uses effective tax rate measures constructed with pretax book income to infer firms' tax avoidance behavior. Because these measures combine cash tax payments with reported accounting income, they may respond to reporting choices as well as to underlying tax payments. This study examines whether commonly used effective tax rate measures yield inferences that reflect underlying tax behavior. We implement a discrimination approach that exploits the differential sensitivity of book-income-based and cash-flow-based effective tax rate measures to accrual-based reporting choices. Using institutional investor site visits in China from 2012 to 2021 as a setting in which reporting incentives plausibly vary, we find that site visit exposure is associated with a significant increase in book-income-based effective tax rates but has no effect on cash-flow-based measures. Decomposition tests show that cash taxes paid remain unchanged, while reported pretax income declines. Thus, a conventional interpretation of book-income-based effective tax rates would imply lower tax avoidance, but this inference is not supported by measures that better isolate underlying tax payments. The evidence indicates that widely used accounting-based tax measures can reflect reportinginduced variation in reported income rather than changes in underlying tax payments. More broadly, the findings highlight an inference problem in empirical research using accounting-based proxies: when such measures respond to reporting choices, they may not reliably capture the underlying economic constructs they are intended to measure.

title: Enhancing Sustainable Performance through Green HRM: The Moderating and Mediating Roles of Green Skills and Competencies in Indonesia's Public Broadcasting Sector

detail.title: Enhancing Sustainable Performance through Green HRM: The Moderating and Mediating Roles of Green Skills and Competencies in Indonesia's Public Broadcasting Sector
detail.abstract: This study examines the role of Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) in enhancing Sustainable Performance within a public broadcasting institution, with a focus on the mediating role of Green Competencies and the moderating effect of Green Skills. Grounded in the Ability-Motivation-Opportunity (AMO) framework, the study uses SmartPLS 4 to analyze data collected from 162 employees of TVRI, Indonesia's national public broadcaster. Results show that GHRM has a positive and significant effect on Sustainable Performance, both directly and through Green Competencies (β = 0.251; p = 0.0419), although the effect sizes remain modest. Green Skills significantly moderate the relationship between GHRM and both Sustainable Performance (β = 0.207; p = 0.046) and Green Competencies (β = 0.191; p = 0.031), reinforcing their strategic importance in translating HR policies into measurable environmental outcomes. The findings contribute theoretically by positioning Green Competencies as both outcome and mechanism within sustainability-focused HR models and offer managerial insights for integrating green HR practices into public sector strategy. Limitations and directions for future research are also discussed.

title: The AI-Augmented Product Manager: How Generative AI Is Reshaping Product Discovery, Strategy, and Execution
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The AI-Augmented Product Manager: How Generative AI Is Reshaping Product Discovery, Strategy, and Execution
detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is changing the role of the product manager. Product managers have traditionally worked at the intersection of customer needs, business goals, technical feasibility, and cross-functional execution. That role remains important, but the work inside the role is changing. Tasks that once required significant manual effort, including customer research synthesis, competitive analysis, product documentation, roadmap preparation, prototype exploration, and stakeholder communication, can now be accelerated through AI-assisted workflows. This paper examines how generative AI is reshaping product management as a knowledge-work function. It argues that AI does not remove the need for product judgment. Instead, it changes where product managers create value. The emerging product manager must become stronger at problem framing, evidence evaluation, strategic prioritization, responsible experimentation, stakeholder alignment, and decision accountability. AI can support analysis, ideation, and execution, but it cannot own the product outcome. Human product leadership remains essential because product management requires judgment under uncertainty, ethical trade-offs, organizational alignment, and accountability for market and user impact. The paper proposes a practical framework for the AI-augmented product manager across five domains: discovery, strategy, execution, communication, and governance. It also identifies risks, including overreliance on AI-generated outputs, shallow validation, biased synthesis, weakened customer empathy, documentation inflation, and unclear accountability. The paper concludes that generative AI will not make product managers obsolete. It will raise the standard for product managers who can combine AI fluency with strong human judgment.

detail.abstract: This paper gives sufficient conditions under which the main equations used in continuous-time heterogeneous-agent macroeconomic models belong to one recursive general equilibrium: the Hamilton−Jacobi−Bellman equation, the conditional-law equation, market-clearing equations, endogenous frontiers, feasibility restrictions, and the transversality condition. The equilibrium-preserving criterion requires value verification, law motion, price determination, frontier determination, law approximation, and finite-horizon truncation to be generated by the same recursive residual system. The main results give a verification theorem, row-level sufficient conditions for existence and local uniqueness, and perturbation results for distributional approximations and finite-horizon truncations. A HANK application puts heterogeneous households, incomplete markets, nominal price rigidity, monetary-fiscal rows, and resource balance in one residual system; it shows how seemingly natural shortcuts−imposed price paths, coarse distribution summaries, and finite-horizon transitions that impose only a terminal value function−can fail to preserve the endogenous feedbacks. The results provide a theorem-level foundation for using Hamilton−Jacobi−Bellman equations in recursive macroeconomic analysis.

title: Sustainability reporting quality evolution: an analysis of Italian banks
affiliations: University of Pavia, University of Pavia, University of Pavia and University of Pavia

detail.title: Sustainability reporting quality evolution: an analysis of Italian banks
detail.abstract: This study examines the evolution and convergence of sustainability reporting quality (SRQ) in the banking sector under a mandatory disclosure regime. Focusing on Italian banks over the period 2017–2023, the analysis investigates whether institutional pressures have improved reporting quality and reduced heterogeneity across institutions. Grounded in institutional theory, the study conceptualizes SRQ as a multidimensional construct, made of completeness, readability, length, and balance. Using a dataset of 257 observations, the study employs longitudinal comparisons and panel data models to assess changes over time and convergence dynamics. The findings provide partial support for an improvement in SRQ, primarily driven by increased environmental disclosure, while social and governance dimensions and textual attributes remain largely stable. Evidence on convergence is mixed, revealing asymmetric patterns: some dimensions converge toward best and other toward worst performers. Overall, the results suggest that regulatory intervention alone is insufficient to ensure homogeneous and substantive sustainability reporting. The study contributes to existing literature on sustainability reporting by offering new evidence on ESG disclosure dynamics in banking and provides implications for regulators and market participants.

title: The Impact of In-Store Overheads and Digital Competition on Consumer Costs

detail.title: The Impact of In-Store Overheads and Digital Competition on Consumer Costs
detail.abstract: This research examines the price gap between physical retail shelves and digital shopping platforms within the Farmington, New Mexico, market. By auditing identical non-food products at local Walmart, Target, and Walgreens locations, this study evaluates how retailers utilize channel-based pricing to manage operational expenses. The analysis indicates that in store consumers pay a significant premium due to lower price elasticity and the high fixed costs of maintaining a local physical presence. The study concludes that navigating these price discrepancies is essential for maintaining household purchasing power in geographically isolated markets.

title: Coordinated Restoration of Transmission and Distribution Systems Considering Frequency Security under Restoration Path Establishment
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Xi'an Jiaotong University (XJTU) - State Key Laboratory of Electrical Insulation and Power Equipment

detail.title: Coordinated Restoration of Transmission and Distribution Systems Considering Frequency Security under Restoration Path Establishment
detail.abstract: The integration of distributed energy resources calls for coordinated restoration of transmission system (TS) and distribution systems (DSs). However, existing researches face challenges in embedding frequency constraints under TS network energization, during which the topology of the restored part is changing. This paper proposes a two-stage strategy for TS and DS restoration. Stage 1 identifies optimal network energization paths from black-start generators to TS loads, forming expanding restoration partitions. Fixing the sequential TS energization paths, stage 2 determines load restoration schemes while explicitly incorporating frequency constraints under both load pickup actions and renewable power fluctuations. To mitigate the impacts of uncertainties from renewable power fluctuations and DS component repair time, a rolling optimization paradigm is applied within stage 2. In both stages, a distributed framework is applied to optimize the utilization of energy resources at the system level and preserve operator independence. An enhanced ADMM algorithm is developed to resolve potential infeasibility issues in existing algorithms with ”Relax-Round-Polish” procedure. Case studies validate the model effectiveness in ensuring frequency security and enabling timely decision-making within each time interval.

title: From Modernization to Easternization: How Permanent Globalization Reshaped Western Societies A Framework for Understanding Western Transformation Introduced by

detail.title: From Modernization to Easternization: How Permanent Globalization Reshaped Western Societies A Framework for Understanding Western Transformation Introduced by

keywords: Modernization – Permanent Globalization – Easternization – Diaspora Politics – Demographic Transformation

detail.abstract: This article argues that the post war Western project of modernization—designed to transform Asia, Africa, and the Middle East through development aid, institution building, and educational exchange—has produced an unexpected reversal. While temporary globalization exported Western models abroad, permanent globalization brought the peoples, cultures, and political concerns of the Global South into Western societies themselves. Through sustained migration, diaspora formation, and demographic permanence, Western countries have become increasingly shaped by influences from the very regions they once sought to modernize. This “Easternization” is not civilizational but structural: it reflects the cumulative effects of settlement, transnational identity, and the spatial and political visibility of diverse communities within Western democracies. By distinguishing between temporary and permanent globalization, the article shows how the West’s outward modernization mission ultimately reshaped its own social fabric, political coalitions, and public spaces. The result is a profound transformation of Western societies—one driven not by the diffusion of Western norms abroad, but by the demographic and cultural return flow of the Global South into the heart of the West.

title: Integrating Green HRM, Competencies, and Leadership for Sustainable Organizational Performance: A Systematic Review

detail.title: Integrating Green HRM, Competencies, and Leadership for Sustainable Organizational Performance: A Systematic Review
detail.abstract: This study aims to review and analyses 24 research articles related to the implementation of Green Human Resource Management (GHRM), green competencies, leadership, and innovation in driving sustainable performance. The selected studies span various sectors, including manufacturing, healthcare, energy, education, and small and medium enterprises (SMEs), utilizing both quantitative and qualitative approaches. The findings reveal that GHRM practices such as green recruitment, green training, environmentally focused performance evaluations, and green compensation significantly influence employee behaviour toward environmentally friendly practices. Furthermore, individual green competencies are proven to enhance green innovation and awareness of environmental and social responsibility. Transformational leadership and a sustainability-driven organizational culture play a critical role in amplifying the impact of GHRM on organizational performance. Several studies also highlight that environmentally conscious workplace design supports the development of adaptive skills and sustainable behaviour. In conclusion, the strategic integration of GHRM, leadership, innovation, and organizational culture significantly contributes to achieving long-term sustainability across diverse industries. The practical implications of this review encourage HR managers and policymakers to embed green values into HR and leadership processes. Future research is recommended to further explore mechanisms and optimal strategies to strengthen the contribution of GHRM in meeting organizational sustainability goals.

title: When Governance Fails Before It Begins: A Model of Narrative Capture in Family Systems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: When Governance Fails Before It Begins: A Model of Narrative Capture in Family Systems
detail.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical model — the Narrative Capture Model (NCM) — to explain why formally sound governance interventions in family firms systematically fail in specific configurations. The central argument is that, in low-institutionalization systems, informational ambiguity is colonized by self-serving narratives from non-contributing members, producing a stable equilibrium that actively resists formalization. The model identifies five core variables, three mechanisms, and five boundary conditions, and generates five testable propositions for future empirical research. Version 1.0 — Working Paper. Propositions are theoretical hypotheses, not validated findings.

title: Technology Terrain: How Systems Inherit Their Own Constraints
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Technology Terrain: How Systems Inherit Their Own Constraints
detail.abstract:
Every technology that works invisibly today was once a choice. This paper introduces Systemic Topography, a framework for understanding how technologies harden from early adoption into irreversible infrastructure.

Drawing on cases spanning global shipping logistics, urban planning, and criminal justice, the framework identifies three distinct terrain types: coordination terrain, which standardizes interfaces; access terrain, which determines who can participate; and fact-producing terrain, which encodes what counts as real within a system. Each type carries its own mechanism of hardening and its own point of intervention.

The paper then turns to artificial intelligence. Machine learning is compressing the timeline between early signal and irreversible terrain, making the window for intervention shorter and harder to observe. At the protocol level, the rapid cross-vendor adoption of the Model Context Protocol illustrates how digital AI systems are already forming new terrain below the threshold of public debate. Within physical AI, automated vehicles, robotic delivery, and AI-enabled security systems are quietly standardizing what machines do, where they operate, and under what conditions. This embedding of new terrain into curb policy, zoning law, and building access is occurring before the implications of that standardization are fully visible.

Systemic Topography is offered as a diagnostic tool for investors, technologists, researchers, and regulators navigating technology decisions at the moment when standards are still being written and terrain is still forming.

detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence accelerates the pace of organizational change, leadership discourse has focused almost exclusively on technological adoption, productivity optimization, and competitive positioning. This paper argues that the dominant metric is being missed entirely. In an AI-accelerated economy, the single most revealing measure of leadership effectiveness is voluntary employee retentionspecifically, the retention of high-performing, emotionally intelligent, creative human talent that no machine can replicate. Drawing on self-determination theory, human capital research, the neuroscience of belonging, and decades of organizational behavior data, this paper proposes that voluntary retention among top-tier talent functions as the definitive performance indicator of leadership quality. It further argues that the philosophically grounded principles of stewardship, genuine human visibility, and deliberate development-not technological fluency-represent the new frame of leadership excellence.

title: Policy-Structured Markets: A Structural Theory of Economic Outcomes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Policy-Structured Markets: A Structural Theory of Economic Outcomes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This is entirely independent and unfunded

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the concept of the policy-structured market to describe contemporary economic systems in which the conditions of competition, capital allocation, and price formation are significantly shaped by government policy settings. While such systems retain the outward appearance of market competition, policy structures systematically influence which actors, business models, and outcomes are able to scale.
The paper develops two mechanisms—Policy Filter and Justification Lock—to explain how policy pathways are selected and stabilised over time. The Policy Filter operates as a pre-decisional selection mechanism, favouring policy types that are structurally compatible with existing institutional and economic arrangements. Justification Lock describes the process through which selected policy pathways are actively reproduced and normalised through repeated justification across policy cycles.
The framework is positioned upstream of existing explanations such as regulatory capture and public choice theory, focusing not on actor influence but on the structural conditions that determine which categories of policy achieve viability. By identifying a coupled feedback dynamic between selection and stabilisation, the paper provides a structural explanation for the persistence and convergence of economic outcomes within formally competitive systems.
The concepts are intended as analytical tools for examining real-world policy environments and understanding how policy structures shape long-term economic trajectories independent of coordination or intent.
