title: Modeling Schedule-Unaware Arrival Behavior at Urban Rail Stations: A Hierarchical Bayesian Bernstein Mixture Model
affiliations: Hongik University and Hongik University

detail.title: Modeling Schedule-Unaware Arrival Behavior at Urban Rail Stations: A Hierarchical Bayesian Bernstein Mixture Model
detail.abstract: Conventional transit waiting-time analyses commonly assume random passenger arrivals, implying uniform arrivals and an expected wait equal to half the headway. Empirical evidence, however, shows that schedule-unaware and schedule-aware arrivals coexist and that their relative composition varies across service and station contexts. Existing mixture models capture this distinction but typically rely on restrictive parametric forms for the planned component and rarely explain the mixing weight using observable covariates; identifiability also remains a concern. This study develops a hierarchical Bayesian mixture model in which the schedule-aware component is represented by a structured Bernstein density, while the schedule-unaware mixing weight is modeled through hierarchical logistic regression on service, station, demand, and time-of-day covariates. The structured weights discourage diffuse near-uniform planned densities, improving separation between the uniform and planned components without claiming global point identification. The model is applied to weekday automated fare collection data from the Seoul metropolitan subway network, organized into station–time-of-day–direction groups. The estimated schedule-unaware ratio varies widely across the network, indicating that neither a purely random-arrival nor a purely schedule-aware assumption adequately represents passenger behavior. Mean headway is the strongest predictor, with a stronger effect during peak periods; underground depth, station exits, peak-period ridership, and time-of-day asymmetries provide additional explanatory power. Sensitivity analysis with a Beta–uniform mixture benchmark shows that similar total density fit can mask different component allocations, underscoring the need for a flexible but structured planned density. The framework supports context-sensitive waiting-time evaluation using routinely collected AFC data.

title: MEASURES OF EFFECTIVENESS FOR QUEUES M/G/1 WHEN THE SERVICE-TIME HAS INFINITE VARIANCE
affiliations: Autonomous University of Barcelona

detail.title: MEASURES OF EFFECTIVENESS FOR QUEUES M/G/1 WHEN THE SERVICE-TIME HAS INFINITE VARIANCE
detail.abstract: This paper introduces novel measures of effectiveness for M/G/1 queues, which are defined in order to encompass the case where the service-time has infinite variance. In a similar way to the traditional measures of performance L=E[N] and W=E[T], we define L (-1)=E[(N+1)-1] and W(-1)=E[T-1], which, contrary to L and W, can remain finite for service-time distributions with infinite variance. These measures are easily computable by integrating the Laplace-Stieltjes transform of the (stationary) waiting-time distribution. We illustrate the use of L(-1) and W(-1) when the service-time obeys an inverse-gamma distribution.

title: Research on regulating capacity market mechanism and clearing modeling method considering the flexibility of system capacity response
affiliations: North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University and North China Electric Power University

detail.title: Research on regulating capacity market mechanism and clearing modeling method considering the flexibility of system capacity response
detail.abstract: Guided by energy security strategies and the objectives of building a new power system, the grid integration of a high proportion of renewable energy and a vast number of diverse demand-side entities has significantly increased the randomness and uncertainty of the power system, leading to profound changes in the balance between supply and demand and in the system's interactive characteristics. This not only results in increasingly tight peak supply capacity but also places higher demands on the flexible response capabilities of various capacity types, such as frequency ragulating capacity, ramping capacity, and reserve capacity. Currently, China's power system remains constrained by the absence of a capacity market mechanism in ensuring capacity response flexibility and the optimal allocation of capacity resources. There is an urgent need to conduct research and design a regulating capacity market aimed at enhancing system flexibility, taking into account the current state of China's power market development. In light of this, this paper investigates the cascading substitution characteristics of multiple capacity types including electric energy capacity, frequency ragulating capacity, ramping capacity, and reserve capacity and proposes calculation methods for the cascading substitution coefficients and demand adjustments. Based on this, the paper designs key mechanisms for a regulating capacity market that accounts for the demand of multiple capacity types, constructs a coordinated clearing model for the regulating capacity market, and proposes a clearing solution method for the regulating capacity market. Furthermore, through case studies, this paper verifies that the designed regulating capacity market by enabling unified bidding and coordinated clearing of electric energy, frequency ragulating capacity, ramping capacity, and reserve capacity can simultaneously ensure system capacity adequacy and flexibility objectives. The research findings presented in this paper provide a reference framework for designing capacity market mechanisms that supplement and optimize the flexibility requirements of various types of capacity response under China's new power system.

title: Generations at Work: Challenges of Multigenerational Coexistence in a Single Department
affiliations: American College, Nicosia

detail.title: Generations at Work: Challenges of Multigenerational Coexistence in a Single Department
detail.abstract: Four distinct generations, ranging from Baby Boomers to Generation Z, are currently working and interacting within the same organizational units, exchanging knowledge and experiences. This study explores the conditions under which multiple generations effectively coexist, collaborate, and innovate, and maintain high productivity within a single organizational department.  Additionally, this study examines the managerial challenges associated with multigenerational diversity. A qualitative methodology was employed based on in-depth interviews with one departmental manager from two different organizational contexts in the private sector: a highly structured, large organization and a less structured medium-sized organization. The findings suggest that multigenerational coexistence is feasible but strongly mediated by organizational culture and leadership practices. In structured environments with clear accountability mechanisms, multigenerational teams exhibited high levels of collaboration, productivity, and minimal conflict. In contrast, less structured managed environments amplify tensions, productivity disparities, and unresolved conflicts.  Perceived generational differences, particularly regarding work values and commitment, appear to be shaped by evolving psychological contracts and institutional reinforcement systems rather than fixed cohort characteristics. Organizations should strengthen governance structures, clarify performance expectations, and equip managers with adaptive leadership skills to effectively manage generational diversity. Overall, this study contributes to generational diversity literature by shifting the focus from deterministic cohort traits to contextual and structural mediators of multigenerational workplace outcomes.

title: Approach or Avoid? The Emergence of Feedback-Seeking in Nascent Entrepreneurship
affiliations: Ansbach University of Applied Sciences, University of Bayreuth, University of Bayreuth and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Approach or Avoid? The Emergence of Feedback-Seeking in Nascent Entrepreneurship
detail.abstract: Although feedback is essential for evaluating early-stage venture ideas, nascent entrepreneurs do not always seek it directly. We examine entrepreneurial feedback seeking as a motivated decision shaped by approach- and avoidance-oriented cues and by individual differences in reinforcement sensitivity. Drawing on Reinforcement Sensitivity Theory, we distinguish between explicit inquiry and implicit monitoring and examine the Behavioral Inhibition System (BIS), which reflects threat sensitivity, and the Behavioral Activation System (BAS), which reflects reward sensitivity. In a metric conjoint experiment with 128 nascent entrepreneurs and 2,048 decisions, approach-oriented cues increased both modes, whereas avoidance-oriented cues reduced explicit inquiry but did not significantly affect implicit monitoring. BIS sensitivity strengthened the negative effects of avoidance-oriented cues on explicit inquiry; BAS sensitivity did not moderate these effects. The findings reveal when nascent entrepreneurs activate explicit inquiry versus implicit monitoring and why motivational sensitivity lead individuals to respond differently to the same venture contexts. ​

title: Improving MR Interaction through Gen AI
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Amity University Kolkata and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Improving MR Interaction through Gen AI
detail.abstract: Mixed Reality (MR) systems integrate digital guidance with physical environments to supportindustrial task execution; however, reliable object detection remains challenging due to occlusion, lighting variation, and limited annotated data. This work addresses data scarcity through diffusion based generative augmentation that expands low-resource industrial datasets with realistic synthetic tool instances under diverse background and illumination conditions, targeting detection failure cases. To validate the effectiveness of the synthetic dataset beyond offline detection metrics, this work conducts a user study in a real MR task execution setting, where detection stability affects the alignment and usability of visual guidance. The study compares three MR assistance modes, Textual Guidance, Bounding Box Guidance, and Holographic Guidance, to assess their impact on user performance, cognitive workload, and usability across varying lighting conditions. Results show that hologram guidance improve visual search time and task performance, with holographic guidancereducing task completion time by 21.4% and workload by 41.9% relative to textual guidance, while increasing usability by 33.4%. These findings demonstrate that diffusion-augmented synthetic data improves object detection robustness and translates into measurable gains in human-centered MR task performance.

title: Passive Leadership as Ethical Omission: A Hybrid Review and Future Agenda
affiliations: Goa Institute of Management

detail.title: Passive Leadership as Ethical Omission: A Hybrid Review and Future Agenda
detail.abstract: Characterized by inaction, avoidance, and disengagement, passive leadership is a consequential type of leadership often related with leadership failure. Despite its prevalence, extant research is fragmented, conceptually ambiguous, and largely disconnected from ethical theorization. Using a hybrid review approach by conducting a bibliometric mapping of articles published in 35 years, this study develops a theory-driven integrative framework. It then uses integrative literature review of the core studies to combine the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) model, Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, and the ethics of omission perspective. Based on insights from this review, a multilevel theoretical model namely Passive Leadership–Resource–Ethics Model (PL-REM) emerged providing the mechanism through which passive leadership affects JD-R, triggers resource loss spirals, and results in moral failure. The article discusses theoretical and practical implications of PL-REM.

title: Neurodiversity Leadership Scale: Conceptualizing and Measuring the Coordination of Cognitive Diversity
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Neurodiversity Leadership Scale: Conceptualizing and Measuring the Coordination of Cognitive Diversity
detail.abstract: Organizations have increasingly recognized the importance of neurodiversity; however,leadership research still lacks robust instruments to capture how leaders effectivelymanage cognitive heterogeneity in the workplace. Existing leadership models primarilyemphasize relational and motivational processes, offering limited attention to systematicdifferences in cognitive functioning. This study conceptualizes and validates theNeurodiversity Leadership Scale (NLS), a multidimensional measure designed to assessleadership competencies related to recognizing, interpreting, and coordinating diversecognitive profiles. The research comprises three complementary studies. Study 1established content validity through expert evaluation. Study 2 examined the latentstructure using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, combined with itemresponse theory. Results also indicated a strong general factor, consistent with ahierarchical structure. Study 3 provided evidence of convergent validity throughtheoretically aligned associations with leadership and organizational variables. Findingssuggest that leadership in cognitively diverse contexts involves not only relationalcompetencies but also the ability to coordinate heterogeneous cognitive styles throughstructural and procedural adaptations. The NLS offers a psychometrically robust tool foradvancing research and practice in cognitively inclusive leadership.

title: DIVERSIFICATION BY PROXY: SCOPE EXPANSION IN PLATFORM ECOSYSTEMS
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Bayes Business School (formerly Cass), City, University of London, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU) - Faculty of Business Administration (Munich School of Management) and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: DIVERSIFICATION BY PROXY: SCOPE EXPANSION IN PLATFORM ECOSYSTEMS
detail.abstract: Digital technologies are transforming the logic of corporate diversification, decoupling scope expansion from asset ownership and enabling firms to extend their reach through orchestrated connections across platforms and ecosystems. We examine this shift in the context of platform ecosystems, where complementors face a distinctive competitive threat: platform owners entering their product space with proprietary offerings. We theorize that complementors’ horizontal scope—both internally constructed through owned assets and externally orchestrated through cross-application connections within the ecosystem—shapes their capacity to absorb competitive pressure and sustain innovation. Using a difference-in-differences design around Apple’s September 2020 announcement of Apple Fitness+, we study how third-party developers in the iOS Health & Fitness category responded to this competitive shock. Directly exposed developers reduce innovation in their existing applications following platform owner entry, but this effect is significantly attenuated for those with broader internal or external scope. We contribute to research on diversification by identifying “diversification by proxy,” i.e., scope expansion through orchestrated external connections rather than owned assets, as an understudied competitive response that operates beyond firm boundaries and reflects the growing role of strategic synergies in the digital age. This also offers practical guidance for third-party developers navigating ecosystems in which the platform owner is also a potential competitor.

title: Leadership Team Educational Diversity and Organizational Resilience: A Leadership Cognition Perspective
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Leadership Team Educational Diversity and Organizational Resilience: A Leadership Cognition Perspective
detail.abstract: Leadership research increasingly emphasizes how leadership teams interpret uncertainty and coordinate adaptive responses. However, less is known about how variation in top management team (TMT) composition shapes these processes and influences organizational resilience. Drawing on upper echelons theory (Hambrick & Mason, 1984) and integrating insights from leadership cognition and social identity perspectives (Lord & Hall, 2005; Tajfel & Turner, 1979), this study examines whether educational and gender diversity differentially relate to organizational resilience. Using cross-sectional survey data from 129 managers in healthcare and education organizations, results indicate that educational diversity within TMTs is positively associated with organizational resilience, whereas gender diversity shows no significant direct relationship. These findings suggest that deep-level diversity contributes to resilience by expanding leadership teams’ cognitive resources and enabling more adaptive decision-making under uncertainty (Simon, 1947; Schubert & Tavassoli, 2020). In contrast, surface-level diversity may not translate into leadership-relevant outcomes absent integrative processes. By reframing diversity as a leadership cognition mechanism, this study extends leadership research by demonstrating how variation in leadership team composition shapes adaptive organizational capacity.

title: Strategic Entry Pathways Across Sectors in Digital Platform Ecosystems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Surrey, Beedie School of Business, Simon Fraser University (SFU) and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Strategic Entry Pathways Across Sectors in Digital Platform Ecosystems
detail.abstract: Digital platform firms increasingly expand beyond their core sectors, yet the strategic pathways through which they enter new markets and create value for producers and buyers remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on a multiple-case study of three digital platform ecosystems, 3D printing, online payments, and smartphones, spanning emerging, growing, and mature lifecycle stages, our inductive analysis reveals four distinct pathways for cross-sector entry. The strategic entry pathways are: (1) value extension – value arising from redeploying existing assets as complements in a target sector; (2) value creation – new utilities for producers and buyers created through new complements or platforms in a target sector; (3) value aggregation – value arising from bundling dispersed third-party offerings from adjacent sectors; and (4) value integration – value arising from interdependencies between complementary offerings across sectors. These entry pathways show how firms leverage digitization, adopt multi-role positions as platform owners and complementors, and build interdependent relationships with incumbents and other ecosystem participants to navigate sectoral boundaries. In doing so, they reconfigure value creation structures and coordination dynamics across sectors. Across the three ecosystem contexts, we show that the same four entry pathways emerge without a prescribed sequence, demonstrating that cross-sector expansion follows distinct but context-independent strategic logics of value creation and coordination. This study contributes to platform and ecosystem strategy literatures by clarifying how cross-sector expansion unfolds, highlighting distinct configurations of value creation, and offering actionable insights for firms pursuing growth beyond their core domains.

title: Arbitration Hacked: Toward a Unified Cybersecurity and Data Breach Framework for International Arbitral Proceedings
affiliations: New York Law School

detail.title: Arbitration Hacked: Toward a Unified Cybersecurity and Data Breach Framework for International Arbitral Proceedings
detail.abstract:
In July 2015, state-sponsored actors compromised the digital infrastructure of the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague during the South China Sea arbitration proceedings, one of the most politically sensitive investment disputes of the twenty-first century. The PCA, administrator of dozens of high-value commercial and investor-state arbitrations, was not a peripheral target. It was chosen because of what it held: state correspondence, litigation strategy, confidential government communications, and the personal data of senior officials, ministers, and counsel. That breach occurred four years before the same institution administered an arbitration in which a tribunal dismissed all applicable data protection obligations in a single paragraph.

International arbitration is a uniquely attractive target for sophisticated adversaries. Arbitral proceedings routinely process state secrets, trade secrets, personal data of corporate executives and government officials, privileged legal communications, financial records, and geopolitically sensitive documents. They process them across a digitally distributed infrastructure involving counsel in multiple countries, institutions in multiple jurisdictions, and third-party service providers, including cloud platforms, transcription services, e-disclosure vendors, and translation tools. The cybersecurity obligations governing this infrastructure are fragmented, the applicable frameworks are inconsistent, and no mandatory unified standard currently exists.

This article proposes the Digital Security Framework (DSF): a unified cybersecurity and data breach protocol for international arbitral proceedings. The DSF synthesizes five source frameworks, namely the ICCA-NYC Bar-CPR Cybersecurity Protocol (2020), the Debevoise & Plimpton protocols, the ICCA-IBA Roadmap on Data Protection (2022), the CPR Cybersecurity Toolkit (2022), and the mandatory breach notification obligations under GDPR Articles 32 to 34, into a single coherent architecture addressable through Procedural Order No. 1. The article critically assesses each source framework, identifies the systematic gaps in the existing patchwork, and proposes a model procedural clause and breach response protocol. It also examines three rapidly evolving technological developments that reshape the cybersecurity obligation landscape: the transition to post-quantum cryptographic standards following the release of NIST FIPS 203, 204, and 205 in August 2024; the rise of the Anthropic Model Context Protocol as a standardized connector between AI systems and enterprise data, together with the architectural vulnerabilities disclosed in that protocol in April 2026; and the April 2026 disclosure of the Anthropic Mythos model, which demonstrated for the first time that a frontier AI system can autonomously identify and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities in every major operating system and web browser, a development that prompted emergency regulatory review by the Financial Stability Board, the Federal Reserve, and the US Treasury.

This article is the third of three companion articles constituting what the author terms the Digital Procedural Constitution of international arbitration. The first article establishes the lex data framework governing data protection obligations. The second establishes the lex AI framework governing mandatory AI governance. Together, the three articles establish that every modern international arbitration simultaneously operates within three coequal mandatory legal frameworks, namely lex arbitri, lex data, and lex AI, supported by an integrated cybersecurity and incident response protocol. The digital hearing room is not secure by default. Securing it is a legal obligation, not a technical preference.

title: The Substrate Problem: Why RAG Observability in Financial Services Requires Infrastructure-Level Verification.

detail.title: The Substrate Problem: Why RAG Observability in Financial Services Requires Infrastructure-Level Verification.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial relationships with any organization that could be perceived to have influenced this research. The onchain analysis was conducted independently using publicly available blockchain data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently.

detail.abstract:
Generative AI systems deployed in financial services increasingly rely on retrieval-augmented generation to ground their outputs in live compliance registries, policy databases, and regulatory documents. The explainability and monitoring literature has responded by developing frameworks for hallucination detection, chain-of-thought validation, and groundedness scoring. These frameworks share a common assumption: that the retrieval layer supplies the model with factually sound and structurally interpretable content. This paper argues that assumption is unwarranted and demonstrates why it matters.

The substrate problem is introduced here as the condition in which a RAG system retrieves content that is internally consistent, authoritative in origin, and structurally complex in ways that a general-purpose model cannot resolve without domain-level interpretive context. Under this condition, a model can reason correctly over what it retrieved and still produce a compliance output that is wrong. No existing monitoring framework identified in this review addresses this failure mode because none extend their observability to the retrieved state itself.

Empirical evidence is drawn from onchain analysis of Tempo's Moderato testnet, a Stripe and Paradigm-backed institutional payments chain, documenting three infrastructure states that instantiate the substrate problem across its compliance architecture. Each state maps to a class of retrieval failure invisible to current RAG monitoring approaches.

From this evidence I derive a three-function retrieval verification layer with a formal pseudocode specification and propose it as a necessary architectural addition to financial RAG systems. The proposal is mapped against EU AI Act Articles 10 and 13, FCA accountability guidance, and PRA SS1/23, identifying the regulatory gaps it addresses. The paper concludes by examining why the substrate problem is most consequential in emerging financial markets and what open questions it surfaces for the field.

title: HOW MULTI-BUSINESS FIRMS EMBRACE PLATFORM DIVERSIFICATION: A PROCESS STUDY
affiliations: University of Glasgow and Delft University of Technology

detail.title: HOW MULTI-BUSINESS FIRMS EMBRACE PLATFORM DIVERSIFICATION: A PROCESS STUDY
detail.abstract: How do multi-business firms create, extend, and modify their platform strategy for digital diversification to connect related and unrelated markets? Platform diversification is emerging as an concept to describe how multi-business firms pursue platform strategies, yet little is known about how these corporations navigate the dual challenge of transforming a diversified, industrial portfolio from product to platform logic. Using dynamic capabilities theory, we conduct a qualitative longitudinal analysis of Siemens (2007–2026), showing how a diversified industrial conglomerate transitions to industrial software platform leadership through a corporate-wide platform diversification strategy. Our analysis reveals four platform diversification capabilities – platform rescoping, platform layering, platform scaling, and platform reconfiguring – deployed across three distinct phases. We develop a recursive process model of platform diversification and introduce generative and convergent platform diversification as two empirically grounded modes, each explaining a different form of corporate scope extension in the digital age. In doing so, we contribute to the corporate strategy and platform strategy literature by extending dynamic capabilities theory to corporate-wide platform diversification, conceptualizing platform diversification as a distinct type of digital diversification.

title: Platform Diversification and Institutional Relatedness
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Chalmers University of Technology

detail.title: Platform Diversification and Institutional Relatedness
detail.abstract: Digital platforms are often portrayed as uniquely capable of diversifying beyond their original domains because modular architectures, reusable data, AI, and network effects reduce the costs of scope expansion. This article challenges and extends this view by examining platform diversification in institutionally dense sectors, where expansion depends not only on technological and market relatedness but also on institutional relatedness. Based on a comparative longitudinal case study of two digital healthcare platforms, we show how regulatory, professional, and stakeholder arrangements shape the feasibility and direction of platform scope expansion. Our findings make three contributions. First, we introduce institutional relatedness as a central dimension of platform diversification, showing that activities can be technologically related yet institutionally distant. Second, we show that institutional relatedness is move-specific: it varies across product, technological, geographic, and business-model dimensions rather than being fixed at the level of the firm, sector, or country. Third, we show that platform diversification in institutionally dense sectors evolves through oscillatory scope evolution, as firms expand along some dimensions while narrowing or refocusing along others. This process is shaped by institutional learning, through which platforms accumulate knowledge about how to operate within specific institutional environments and thereby reshape what future diversification moves become feasible. The study advances a more institutionally grounded understanding of diversification in the digital age.

title: Stock Predictor: A Web Based App With Live Trends
affiliations: NIST University, NIST University, NIST University, NIST University and NIST University

detail.title: Stock Predictor: A Web Based App With Live Trends
detail.abstract: This paper tells us about a stock predicting web-based application which uses machine learning techniques that is combined with a real time financial data visualization. The objective of this web-based project is to help the users in understanding stock market behavior and allowing them to make basic buy/sell decisions. This application uses a pre-trained machine learning model which predicts whether stock price will rise or fall. It uses two key features: Open-Close difference and High-Low difference. The app uses Streamlit for the user-interface and it fetches the real time stock data from yFinance API and plotly for better data visualization. It also helps the users globally by supporting multi-currency conversion. It has a live dashboard which displays top performing stocks and how the daily price changes. The model which is used is simple and demonstrates the implementation of machine learning and financial prediction systems. It integrates data science, web development and financial analytics together to form a single platform. It can be further improved by using advanced models and features.

title: Freight Transport Carbon Footprint Under Uncertainty: A Regional Scenario Analysis
affiliations: University of Graz, University of Graz and Institute of Systems Sciences, Innovation and Sustainability Research

detail.title: Freight Transport Carbon Footprint Under Uncertainty: A Regional Scenario Analysis
detail.abstract: This study quantifies the life-cycle carbon footprint of regional freight transport under three decarbonisation scenarios while systematically accounting for uncertainties. Using Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) with Monte Carlo simulation (applied to freight scenario analysis for the first time) three 2040 policy scenarios with escalating ambition are evaluated for the Austrian region of Styria, capturing vehicle production, energy supply, infrastructure, and operations. Even the most ambitious scenario, which eliminates all direct emissions and holds freight demand constant, achieves only a 36% reduction from the status quo, with over one million tonnes CO₂-equivalent remaining annually. This residual footprint is dominated by infrastructure and vehicle manufacturing emissions that persist regardless of operational decarbonisation, accounting for up to 76% of total emissions. Uncertainty analysis reveals that moderate policy measures are statistically indistinguishable from business-as-usual under unfavourable conditions. These findings demonstrate that freight decarbonisation requires cross-sectoral industrial transformation beyond the reach of transport policy alone.

title: Do Transformers Always Win? An Empirical Study of Semantic Embeddings for Short-Text E-commerce Reviews
affiliations: University of Rochester, Stanford University,  and Northeastern University (USA)

detail.title: Do Transformers Always Win? An Empirical Study of Semantic Embeddings for Short-Text E-commerce Reviews

publicationDetails.detailsText: Accepted and are currently in press with IEEE ISBDAS 2026(ISBN: 979-8-3315-7218-1)

detail.abstract: While transformer-based embeddings like Sentence-BERT have become the de facto standard for text representation, their performance on short, noisy industrial texts has received limited empirical scrutiny. This study compares TF-IDF, Word2Vec, and Sentence-BERT on clustering 100,000 Amazon product reviews. Our findings challenge prevailing assumptions: Word2Vec achieves superior clustering performance with a Silhouette score of 0.1828 versus SBERT's 0.0401, representing a 356% improvement. We attribute this to insufficient text length for contextual modeling, domain mismatch between pre-training corpora and e-commerce reviews, and destabilizing variance in cluster centroids from contextualized representations. For topic modeling, Non-negative Matrix Factorization with Count Vectorizer achieves highest coherence (Cv=0.5836), while Latent Dirichlet Allocation produces most balanced distributions. These results suggest classical methods offer compelling costperformance advantages for short industrial texts.

title: Learning Model Orchestration: Beyond Personalization in the Age of AI

detail.abstract: For most of modern educational history, advanced learning arrangements have been structurally scarce. The majority of learners have had access to only a narrow band of instructional forms, most notably collective teacher-led instruction and unsupported self-study. By contrast, elite educational settings have often provided not merely better content, but richer combinations of learning models: guided questioning, individualized feedback, apprenticeship-like coaching, iterative practice, and adaptive pacing. This paper argues that artificial intelligence changes education most fundamentally not by making information more available, but by expanding access to multiple learning models and by lowering the cost of combining them. To describe this shift, the paper introduces the concept of Learning Model Orchestration (LMO): the intentional selection, sequencing, and combination of different learning models in ways that fit a learner's goals, developmental stage, cognitive state, and constraints of time and energy. The paper develops four claims. First, educational inequality has long included a hidden dimension: unequal access to advanced learning models. Second, AI expands the practical availability of learning interactions such as explanation, questioning, simulation, feedback, and guided practice. Third, the central educational problem therefore shifts from access to information toward orchestration under abundance. Fourth, this shift may generate a new fault line of inequality: orchestration inequality, or unequal capacity to design and govern effective learning architectures. Rather than treating AI primarily as a teacher substitute, this paper reframes AI as infrastructure for expanding the learning model space available to ordinary learners. The future of education, on this view, will depend less on whether AI is present than on whether learners, families, educators, and institutions can orchestrate learning models well. The educational frontier is thus moving not simply from scarcity to abundance, but from information access to the design of learning architectures under cognitive constraints.

title: Generative AI and Information Warfare: Outlining a Policy Framework to Counteract Foreign Influence Operations in the New Age of Disinformation

detail.title: Generative AI and Information Warfare: Outlining a Policy Framework to Counteract Foreign Influence Operations in the New Age of Disinformation
detail.abstract: This paper examines the emerging threat of generative AI-powered foreign influence operations and proposes a comprehensive policy framework for the United States to counter them. First, I analyze how advances in generative AI, particularly in synthetic media generation and autonomous decision-making, are transforming the economics and capabilities of social media-based influence operations. I then evaluate the influence operation capabilities and strategic objectives of four primary adversary nations: China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, and assess how these advancements will transform their ability to conduct information warfare against democratic societies. From this threat assessment, I evaluate technical mitigation strategies at four key stages of the influence operation lifecycle: model availability, model access, content dissemination, and belief formation. I assess each of these interventions, including radioactive data watermarking, content provenance standards such as C2PA, platform authentication requirements, and detection model deployment, on its feasibility, effectiveness, and vulnerability to circumvention. From this analysis, I propose a broader policy response - a full legislative and institutional mitigation framework centered on three tenets: maintaining American AI superiority through strategic export controls and compute governance, building public-private partnerships between government agencies and technology platforms, and cultivating societal resilience through media literacy and civic education initiatives. The paper concludes that effective mitigation will require coordinated action between AI developers, social media companies, and government agencies, and that no single intervention point is sufficient in isolation.

title: An Integrated Knowledge-Based Decision Support System for Precision Livestock Nutrition: Hybrid Reasoning from Small-Sample Experimental Data on Silage Ramie Substitution in Xiangxi Yellow Cattle
affiliations: Hunan Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Hunan Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Hunan Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Zhejiang University - Institute of Dairy Science, Hunan Institute of Animal and Veterinary Science, Hunan Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Hunan Institute of Animal and Veterinary Science and Hunan Academy of Agricultural Sciences

detail.title: An Integrated Knowledge-Based Decision Support System for Precision Livestock Nutrition: Hybrid Reasoning from Small-Sample Experimental Data on Silage Ramie Substitution in Xiangxi Yellow Cattle
detail.abstract: The paradigm of precision livestock farming (PLF) demands intelligent decision support systems (DSS) capable of translating complex, multi-dimensional biological data into actionable nutritional strategies, yet such systems are frequently constrained by small-sample, high-dimensional datasets typical of controlled feeding trials. This paper presents an integrated knowledge-based DSS for optimizing livestock nutrition, demonstrated through a case study on substituting silage corn with silage ramie (Boehmeria nivea L.) in the diet of Xiangxi Yellow Cattle. The system employs a hybrid reasoning framework synergistically combining three inference paradigms: a forward-chaining production rule engine grounded in statistically validated findings, a case-based reasoning (CBR) module leveraging individual animal records, and an ensemble machine learning (ML) predictor utilizing Random Forest and Gradient Boosting algorithms, with a meta-reasoning layer dynamically fusing outputs via context-dependent confidence assessments. The knowledge base was constructed from a controlled trial involving 21 cattle across five dietary groups, yielding 11 production rules and a 21-record case library. Leave-one-out cross-validation confirmed strong ML predictive performance for diet-sensitive serum biomarkers (SOD: R2=0.791; CAT: R2=0.545) but poor generalization for complex production traits (net meat rate: R2=−0.263), empirically validating the hybrid architecture. The system confirmed that complete silage ramie substitution significantly enhances antioxidant capacity (CAT: +15.4%, P=0.0005; SOD: +174.5%, P=0.0002; T-AOC: +14.7%, P=0.0008) and immune function (IgA: +45.1%; IgG: +41.8%, P=0.0005) while reducing lipid peroxidation (MDA: −51.5%, P=0.0065), alongside a modest decrease in slaughter rate (−3.2%, P=0.0255). The system is deployed as a RESTful API, providing a replicable framework for transforming experimental findings into dynamic decision-support assets.

title: Open Innovation Strategies for Business Model Innovation: The Moderating Role of Absorptive Capacity
affiliations: Johannes Kepler University Linz, University of St Gallen and University of St Gallen

detail.title: Open Innovation Strategies for Business Model Innovation: The Moderating Role of Absorptive Capacity
detail.abstract: Business model innovation (BMI) is a crucial mechanism that allows firms to adapt to changing market conditions. However, the strategic factors that facilitate such renewal, particularly the distinct roles of different open innovation strategies, require further investigation. This study examines how various forms of open innovation - outside-in, inside-out, and coupled strategies - contribute to BMI and the conditions under which they are most effective. Using survey data from senior executives of established companies, we demonstrate that all three strategies are positively associated with BMI. Furthermore, our findings reveal that absorptive capacity plays a fundamental role. While it significantly strengthens the positive impact of outside-in strategies, it mitigates the effect of inside-out strategies. However, absorptive capacity appears to have no effect on coupled strategies. These results clarify the mixed effects of open innovation on BMI and establish absorptive capacity as a key boundary condition that shapes the pathway to BMI.

title: Structural Pathways to Wildfire Evacuation Planning in the Western United Statess
affiliations: Texas State University, Texas State University, Texas State University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Structural Pathways to Wildfire Evacuation Planning in the Western United Statess
detail.abstract: Wildfire evacuation planning in the western United States remains uneven despite increasing fire risk, yet the structural pathways linking household characteristics to preparedness are still poorly understood. This study applies Structural Equation Modeling to survey data from 853 residents in California, Colorado, and Oregon to examine how household characteristics, mobility resources, prior evacuation experience, and behavioral choices shape formal evacuation planning. Two complementary models are estimated: a latent variable model defining evacuation decision capacity and a path analysis model tracing direct and indirect pathways to planning through behavioral mediators. Results show that vehicle ownership is the strongest driver of evacuation decision capacity, while pet ownership directly increases planning. Prior evacuation experience shortens departure time and promotes self-initiated action, and GPS access influences in-event choices. Evacuation timing is the only significant direct predictor of planning, identifying delayed departure as a critical bottleneck for preparedness.

title: AIScope SG: A Policy-Aware, Bilingual AI Occupational Exposure Index for Singapore

detail.title: AIScope SG: A Policy-Aware, Bilingual AI Occupational Exposure Index for Singapore

detail.abstract: Existing AI occupational exposure indices (Felten, Raj, & Seamans, 2021; Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin, & Rock, 2024; Pizzinelli et al., 2023) anchor on US-centric occupational taxonomies and treat regulatory friction as narrative rather than as a binding scoring constraint. This paper introduces AIScope SG, an open, bilingual (English/Chinese) AI occupational exposure index built on the Singapore Standard Occupational Classification 2024 (SSOC 2024). Covering 570 occupations, AIScope SG encodes three Singaporespecific policy levers as hard constraints in code: (i) the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) cap, which ceilings exposure scores at 4.0 for covered occupations; (ii) a regulatory-moat discount matrix (MOH, MAS, SAL, BCA) grounded in the occupational licensing literature (Kleiner & Krueger, 2013) and Autor's (2015) complementarity framing; and (iii) a GraphRAG-based transition-path generator that surfaces skilladjacent, lower-exposure occupations as reskilling targets, designed to be merged with the official SkillsFuture Skills Framework. We further propose a concrete empirical validation design using MOM's Occupational Employment Dataset to backtest 2020-2025 occupational transitions. The architecture makes exposure scores auditable, policy-coherent, and directly actionable for SkillsFuture and allied reskilling programmes.

title:
Layer 9 - The Missing Top Layer of the Internet 
From Person-Centric Networks to Claim-Native Epistemic Infrastructure
affiliations: Independent

detail.title:
Layer 9 - The Missing Top Layer of the Internet 
From Person-Centric Networks to Claim-Native Epistemic Infrastructure
detail.abstract: The Internet lacks a shared epistemic substrate. Documents can be linked, data transported, and social profiles connected-but claims have no persistent identity, no provenance, no conflict structure, and no social-operational roles across systems. This paper argues that this absence is not a feature deficit-it is a structural architectural gap equivalent in significance to the absence of the application layer itself.

title: Digital Platforms as Catalysts for the International Expansion of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Digital Platforms as Catalysts for the International Expansion of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of digital technologies has significantly transformed the global business landscape. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which historically faced substantial barriers when expanding into international markets, are increasingly benefiting from digital transformation. Limited financial resources, restricted access to international networks, and inadequate knowledge of foreign markets have traditionally constrained the global growth of SMEs (Brouthers et al., 2016). In recent years, digital platforms have emerged as powerful tools that help smaller firms overcome these limitations. Online marketplaces, digital payment systems, and global communication technologies allow SMEs to connect with international customers more efficiently than ever before. As a result, many SMEs are now able to enter foreign markets with lower operational costs and reduced structural barriers (Kenney & Zysman, 2016). This study explores the role of digital platforms in supporting the international expansion of SMEs. By examining existing academic literature and incorporating empirical insights, the research analyzes how digital platforms reduce market entry barriers, improve global connectivity, and assist SMEs in making strategic business decisions. The findings suggest that digital platforms play an increasingly important role in accelerating SME internationalization. At the same time, the research also highlights certain challenges, including increased competition within digital ecosystems and potential dependence on platform-based business models.

detail.abstract: Decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) and AI-agent systems combine cryptographic execution with blockchain-based governance, yet observed organizations almost universally combine these mechanisms with a conventional legal entity-a foundation, statutory DAO form, or limited liability wrapper. I develop a stylized model in which token-holders jointly determine wrapper choice and governance concentration, generating multiple equilibria: an inefficient trap in which the wrapper coalition cannot form because no holder will absorb the front-loaded fixed cost alone, and an efficient wrapper equilibrium in which the coalition reaches scale and amortizes fixed costs effectively. The trap is an empirically grounded coordination problem rather than an analytical artifact, and a global-games selection argument identifies the threshold at which institutional design tips the system between equilibria. The framework reframes the CFTC v. Ooki DAO ruling, the Wyoming DAO LLC and DUNA statutes, and AI legal personhood debates as questions of equilibrium selection rather than of substantive cost allocation, and bounds the "Coasean singularity" claim that AI agents dramatically reduce transaction frictions.

title: Integrated survey of EV charging planning, scheduling, and behavior
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Georgia, University of Louisville and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Integrated survey of EV charging planning, scheduling, and behavior
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles has shifted the key bottleneck from vehicle adoption to charging infrastructure. Deploying charging networks requires coupled decisions across Planning, Scheduling, and Behavior: where and how much to build, how to operate chargers and prices under grid constraints, and how users choose stations and charging times. This survey proposes a three-layer Planning--Scheduling--Behavior (PSB) framework that organizes fragmented EV charging research through explicit coupling edges and an actor taxonomy. We identify a tradeoff between modeling fidelity and computational tractability that we term the P-S-B trilemma: each layer is computationally difficult, and realistic cross-layer integration requires simplifying at least one layer. Reviewing the three pairwise-coupling literatures, we show that the missing third layer is typically fixed exogenously. These simplifications have distinct costs, and the PSB framework makes them explicit to guide which layer to simplify for different planning objectives.

title: From Fair Recovery to Repeat Purchases: Commitment as a Mediator between Justice Perceptions and Repurchase Intentions in E-Retailing
affiliations: University of Kashmir, University of Kashmir and Government of Jammu and Kashmir

detail.title: From Fair Recovery to Repeat Purchases: Commitment as a Mediator between Justice Perceptions and Repurchase Intentions in E-Retailing
detail.abstract: Grounded in the multi-theoretical framework of justice theory, social exchange theory, and Stimulus-organism-response (SOR) paradigm, this study investigates how customers’ perceived justice of service recovery efforts shape their repurchase intentions following service failure. Employing Partial Least Square Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to analyse data from 509 participants, this study advances service recovery literature by finding a direct as well as indirect relationship between perceived justice of service recovery and repurchase intentions. This suggests that, despite experiencing an adverse situation, successful service recovery can reinforce customer’s commitment and foster a favorable attitude towards the e-vendor, reflected in terms of repeat purchases. This study thus advances the prior research by addressing gaps in our understanding of service recovery process and integrating underexplored relational components, such as affective and continuance commitment as mediators. These insights offer a comprehensive and strategic framework for online practitioners to transform service failures into successful resolutions.

title: A Critique of Music Critic Reviews: Evaluating Sentiment Analysis Methods Against Human Judgment
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Critique of Music Critic Reviews: Evaluating Sentiment Analysis Methods Against Human Judgment
detail.abstract: This study examines the consistency between textual and numerical evaluations in professional music album reviews. While consumer reviews have been extensively studied, professional critical opinions remain under-explored. To investigate the alignment between qualitative expressions and numeric assessments, we employ a diverse set of sentiment analysis methods to extract continuous sentiment scores from review texts in both short and full-length forms. We find that extracted sentiment scores vary significantly depending on the method used, the length of the underlying textual input, and the specific model architecture. While correlations between traditional computational models and critic grades remain low to moderate, the generative LLM-as-a-judge model successfully captures nuanced textual sentiment, attaining the highest correlation with human judgment.

title: From Behavioral Traces to Actionable Guidelines: A Comprehensive Survey of Representation, Optimization, and Verifiable Generation in Intelligent Systems

detail.title: From Behavioral Traces to Actionable Guidelines: A Comprehensive Survey of Representation, Optimization, and Verifiable Generation in Intelligent Systems

keywords.keywords: Behavioral trace analysisGuideline generationProcess miningOffline reinforcement learningImitation learningLarge language models (LLMs)Decision-support systemsExplainable artificial intelligence

detail.abstract: Behavioral traces are increasingly captured across enterprise systems, user interfaces, clinical platforms, and embodied environments, creating new opportunities for intelligent systems to move beyond descriptive and predictive analytics toward actionable decision support. However, the relevant literature remains fragmented across process mining, user behavior mining, predictive and prescriptive monitoring, imitation learning, offline reinforcement learning, and large language model (LLM)-based generation.This survey synthesizes these disconnected research streams through a unified framework organized into four stages: behavior representation and abstraction, behavior understanding, behavior optimization, and guideline generation. We define a guideline as a structured, human-readable, and verifiable artifact that specifies applicability conditions, ordered or conditional actions, exceptions, expected effects, and evidence links.Based on this conceptualization, we review the principal methodological families contributing to each stage, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and interactions. We identify the key technical gap as the absence of end-to-end approaches that transform behavioral traces into deployable, evidence-grounded guidance artifacts.We further propose a research agenda centered on causal validity, communicability, robustness under distribution shift, and verification mechanisms for generated guidance (Pearl, 2009; Imbens & Rubin, 2015). The central argument of this survey is that the next generation of intelligent decision-support systems must not only learn predictive or optimal behavior, but also generate structured, auditable, and operationally actionable guidelines grounded in empirical evidence and validated through explicit verification processes.

title: ML-based anomaly detection for streaming pipelines: an empirical benchmark with cross-workload generalization on Apache Kafka and Flink
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: ML-based anomaly detection for streaming pipelines: an empirical benchmark with cross-workload generalization on Apache Kafka and Flink
detail.abstract: Anomaly detection research has largely overlooked streaming-specific failures such as consumer lag spikes, backpressure propagation, and checkpoint degradation. We present an open empirical benchmark on Apache Kafka and Apache Flink telemetry across two controlled cloud-deployed workloads on Amazon EKS (e-commerce at 5,000 events/s, industrial IoT at 10,000 events/s) with eight fault types and 160 runs. Eight semi-supervised models (Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, four reconstruction autoencoders, Deep SVDD, DAGMM) are evaluated alongside supervised Random Forest, a production rule baseline, and a max-z diagnostic at 30s on both workloads (IoT covers 15-300 s) under ten-fold CV. Models train on normal-only data but use labels for HPO and threshold calibration; under that regime they reach F1 of approximately 0.49 at per-fold prevalence (31.9%), but at realistic 1-5% deployment prevalence F1 collapses to 0.02-0.16 with the autoencoder cluster firing 90-105 false alerts/hour, so benchmark F1 overstates deployment performance. A simple EWMA z-residual baseline reaches F1 = 0.527 and outperforms every deep semi-supervised model. Under leave-one-fault-out evaluation the panel collapses to F1 of 0.20 or below across eight held-out faults; full-HPO LOFO on the broker-crash representative produces F1 of 0.08 or below, establishing a generalisation gap to unseen fault classes. Within the two Kafka/Flink workloads studied, per-fault difficulty rankings transfer for reconstruction autoencoders and rule-based methods (Spearman rho > 0.85, N = 8), broker-layer underperformance replicates on IoT, optimal window size is workload-specific, and cross-train transfer drops AUC to approximately 0.50 for most reconstruction models. Datasets and analysis artifacts are released openly.​​
